name: domainry-builder-v1
description: Extract an evidence-backed backend dependency PRD from a delivered frontend, then build, evolve, repair, integrate, and verify the matching Domainry source-owned application through one project-visible development TODO. The Skill keeps frontend evidence read-only while settling requirements and domain truth, authors declarative backend/model/*.json metadata, and records evidence-located frontend defects as findings for the frontend owner instead of repairing them. Use for frontend-to-Runtime replacement, new backend projects, existing-project increments, metadata-first backend implementation, Runtime integration, full-stack defect routing, and final verification.

# Domainry Builder V1

Use exactly this workflow, in this order:

`requirements → model → apply → verify → done`

There is no parallel workflow, receipt attachment ceremony, continuation route, implementation stage, or hidden stage. The project-visible TODO at `.domainry/development/<session-id>.md` is the only progress record. Set its `Current stage` to one of the five names above. Change it only after the current section is complete, and only to the immediate successor.

Resolve `SKILL_ROOT` from this loaded `SKILL.md`, set `DOMAINRY_CLI="$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-cli"`, and run `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" version --json` before other Builder commands. Never discover another Builder CLI through `PATH` or combine files from different Skill installations.

If the session TODO does not exist, copy [DEVELOPMENT_TODO.template.md](assets/DEVELOPMENT_TODO.template.md) to the exact session path and fill its header. If it exists, resume from its `Current stage`; do not create a second workflow or parallel state file.

## requirements

Read [requirements-and-domain-truth.md](references/requirements-and-domain-truth.md) and [BACKEND_REQUIREMENTS_PRD.template.md](assets/BACKEND_REQUIREMENTS_PRD.template.md). Inspect `frontend/**` only when the project actually contains frontend source, and keep it read-only. Settle domain truth inside this stage: actors and scope, objects and state, actions and transaction/idempotency behavior, calculations and settlement, reports and pagination/export, schedules, notifications, files, and integrations. Platform capabilities may inform implementation later; they do not decide business truth.

Write or update `docs/backend-requirements-prd.md`. Do not advance while an unresolved choice changes an observable business result, authorization decision, amount/unit rule, irreversible external effect, or business-state flow.

## model

Read [backend-model.md](references/backend-model.md) and the [capability index](references/capabilities/README.md), then only the capability references needed by the accepted requirements. Author project-owned `backend/model/*.json` and referenced `backend/reports/*.sql`.

Use the embedded CLI for bounded discovery and validation:

```sh
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model capabilities --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model capability --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --key <category>
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model check --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model plan --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
```

## apply

Read [project-mutation.md](references/project-mutation.md). Review the current plan and any destructive/evolution decision. `apply model` is the only normal development release command:

```sh
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" apply model --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" \
  --go-module-path <domain-qualified-module> --product-surfaces <reviewed-surfaces>
```

After materialization, read [ownership-and-extensions.md](references/ownership-and-extensions.md) and implement only the project-owned backend source and tests required by the applied model. Use `apply action-context` or `apply connector-context` for the specific item being implemented. Never create placeholders or edit generated code, manifests, receipts, caches, journals, or Runtime-managed state.

Prepare the delivery-bound implementation packet before editing project source:

```sh
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" apply prepare --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
```

Check and finalize project source with one direct CLI command:

```sh
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" apply finalize --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
```

Implement project business-flow tests and every applicable large-scale fixture
script here, run focused tests while iterating, then run the affected backend
test set before advancing. `verify` executes completed tests and captures
evidence; it must not be the first place an entire test suite is authored.

## verify

Read [evidence-levels.md](references/evidence-levels.md), [verification.md](references/verification.md), [production-verification-checklist.md](references/production-verification-checklist.md), and [backend-runtime.md](references/backend-runtime.md). Run structural verification, package the project, start one managed Runtime, and exercise the accepted real-data scenarios. Frontend build/test remains frontend-owned.

Structural verification/package success cannot establish real-data scenario acceptance. Run the highest-risk semantic canary before broader Runtime scenario integration.

```sh
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" verify structure --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" verify package --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" verify runtime start --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --address 127.0.0.1:<port>
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" verify runtime status --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
```

Treat Runtime identifiers and principal/context values as opaque. Bind acceptance to formal actors, authorization and data scope, durable effects, idempotent replay, denied/error unchanged state, and the current package/database cohort. Stop the managed Runtime when it is no longer needed.

If verification reveals a source defect, return explicitly to the smallest
invalidated apply boundary, repair source and affected tests there, rerun
finalization/structure/package and every stale evidence gate, then re-enter
verify. Never keep the stage labeled verify while first-writing the repaired
business-flow suite. Rebuild a stopped managed SQLite cohort and rotate its
acceptance credentials only with `verify runtime rebuild`; never move or delete
`runtime-process.json`, `runtime.db`, its cohort marker, or acceptance secrets
by hand.

## done

Resolve every in-scope finding, update the TODO to `Current stage: done`, and run the lightweight consistency check:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-todo-check.py" \
  --todo "$PROJECT_ROOT/.domainry/development/$SESSION_ID.md" --expected-stage done
```

Report the delivery identity, changed files, tests, Runtime result, highest evidence level reached, and any explicit non-blocking limitation. Never claim more than the evidence proves.

### Invariants

- One Agent session owns one project TODO through all five stages.
- Requirements and domain truth precede capability mapping.
- `frontend/**` is read-only. Frontend defects are reported to owner `frontend`, not repaired by this Skill.
- Project-owned edits are limited to declarative model/SQL, backend source/tests, requirements PRD, and the current TODO.
- Recoverable command failures stay in the current stage: diagnose, repair the owning source, rerun the direct command, and continue.

# Requirements and domain truth

Use only for the `requirements` TODO section. Produce the accepted backend dependency PRD and freeze domain facts before capability discovery. Do not load model, apply, verification, or acceptance authority at this stage.

## Backend dependency PRD

For a new project or a complete frontend Mock-to-Runtime replacement, create or update `docs/backend-requirements-prd.md` from `assets/BACKEND_REQUIREMENTS_PRD.template.md`. For a light existing-project increment, record an equivalent traceable PRD delta in the current session TODO or update the accepted backend PRD, and reference the unchanged baseline.

A source is structured when its rules live in stable titled/numbered sections citable as `<doc> §N`. If one section states a rule completely, cite it rather than restating it. A reference-mode PRD still carries requirement IDs, classifications, owner/capability mapping, decisions, acceptance criteria, and the matrices, each row citing its source section.

Read frontend evidence, when present, in this order: route/page registry and user journeys; typed application API; Mock adapters/fixtures; state stores and hooks; form/list/detail/report components; permission/menu guards; tests and stories; visible copy. Also read the current explicit requirement and latest accepted product/design documents. Frontend inspection is read-only. Mock or visible behavior proves demand or a current assumption, not a business rule without higher-precedence evidence.

Use this precedence while preserving every conflict:

1. explicit current user decision;
2. latest accepted requirement or design contract;
3. latest implemented frontend behavior;
4. typed API and Mock semantics;
5. frontend tests;
6. legacy/reference implementation.

Classify every item as `confirmed`, `recommended`, `open`, `frontend_only`, or `legacy_reference`. Extract actors, journeys, observable success, objects, fields, relations, queries, commands, states, permissions/scopes, errors/conflicts, calculations, transactions/idempotency, external effects, and presentation-only behavior. Every write operation names authorization, observable validation/error behavior, transaction boundary, idempotency/retry policy, durable result, and acceptance proof.

Build one traceability row per requirement: `demand evidence → requirement ID → Runtime owner/capability → model resource or approved source gap → permission/data scope → acceptance journey`. Account for every backend-bound typed API operation and every route. Matrix cells are phrases; do not repeat table facts in prose.

## Critical ambiguity

Classify every unresolved choice before capability selection. Only `business_blocker` blocks model authoring, and only for the smallest affected slice.

| Decision class | Boundary | Handling | Blocks model? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `business_blocker` | At least two concrete incompatible choices remain, and selecting one changes an explicitly required observable result, authorization allow/deny, amount/unit semantics, irreversible external effect, or business-state flow | Name the choices, affected requirements/model items, and obtain current user or accepted requirement authority | Yes, smallest slice only |
| `contract_discovery` | Runtime-owned formal code, canonical identity/context source, or accepted-fact-to-capability mapping | Defer discovery to the typed client/fixed capability contract; record a Foundation/Runtime gap if absent | No |
| `safe_implementation_decision` | Reversible technical choice preserving the accepted invariant | Defer to the published standard or record one conservative default and evolution path | No |
| `product_follow_up` | Product preference with a fallback that preserves required results | Record assumption, owner, fallback, excluded acceptance scope, and review trigger | No |

Security/privacy omissions default to least privilege, sensitive by default, and no export. An explicit broader-disclosure requirement remains a `business_blocker` until its authorization boundary is confirmed.

Use these nonblocking defaults without inventing product rules:

- Explicit exact decimals, comparisons, or sums do not require absent optional currency/unit/range metadata; block only a comparison/conversion slice where incompatible units change the required result.
- Explicit asynchronous approval may use an independent approval Object while the host remains unchanged until the terminal effect; missing edit/cancel/resubmit preferences are follow-ups.
- An explicitly immutable resource with no required business-role read needs no invented read actor; prove creation through a formal admin/seed path or persistence evidence.
- Weekday/morning intent with no timezone/holiday preference uses deterministic deployment timezone and standard weekday cron; block only explicit incompatible calendar outcomes.

## Domain truth design

Freeze domain facts before asking what Runtime can implement. When requirements contain calculations, historical facts, settlement, correction, or reversal, read [domain-truth-and-settlement.md](domain-truth-and-settlement.md) once and close its ownership, persistence, snapshot, trace, correction, and consumer decisions.

Financial, payroll, points, inventory-cost, and settlement facts remain reproducible after Settings change. If an event locks a result, define the write-side atomic action and immutable snapshot/ledger before its reports.

Before capability discovery, settle these observable Report/export invariants when applicable:

1. List Reports use bounded server pagination, a maximum page size, stable ordering with a unique tie-breaker, an opaque cursor, and explicit `truncated`/`total` semantics.
2. Export uses the same Report, parameters, source hash, authorization, and data Scope; a bounded `0..1000` probe selects synchronous governed CSV or asynchronous paged export.
3. Asynchronous export reauthorizes the current persisted principal before page one and sends requester-only terminal notification.
4. Canonical database compare-and-create reuses accepted/running work or a completed unexpired artifact; `audit_id` is excluded from the fingerprint.

Record the required current-database query-plan evidence and driver (`EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN`, `EXPLAIN FORMAT=JSON`, or `EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON)`) as an acceptance obligation. Capability schemas and G01-G32 technical applicability are deliberately deferred to the model route returned by the machine resume packet.

item.aggregated_output:
# Backend model files

`backend/model/*.json` is the backend metadata inventory and source of truth; `backend/reports/*.sql` is the source-owned SQL surface referenced by Report model items. The Blueprint Ledger under `domain/` and everything under `.domainry/` are CLI-owned projections that `apply model` converges from those sources. Never edit `domain/**`, rendered Blueprints, or `.domainry/**` by hand, and never treat them as an authoring input.

## File contract

Every file under `backend/model/` matching `*.json` is loaded, in lexical filename order:

```json
{
  "contract_version": "domainry-backend-model-v1",
  "items": [
    {
      "module": "project",
      "kind": "project",
      "key": "project",
      "payload": {"blueprint": {"schema_version": "1", "id": "gym", "name": "Gym", "description": "Gym operations"}}
    },
    {
      "module": "membership",
      "kind": "requirement",
      "key": "membership-management",
      "depends_on": ["project/project/project"],
      "payload": {"requirement": {"statement": "Manage membership metadata", "acceptance_criteria": ["Membership metadata validates"], "behaviors": [], "no_executable_behavior_reason": "This minimal file-contract example emits no executable resource"}}
    },
    {
      "module": "membership",
      "kind": "actor_role",
      "key": "membership-roles",
      "requirement_keys": ["membership-management"],
      "depends_on": ["project/project/project", "membership/requirement/membership-management"],
      "payload": {"emits": [{"collection": "roles", "key": "membership_member", "value": {"key": "membership_member", "name": "Membership member", "permissions": [], "record_scope": "all_records"}}]}
    }
  ]
}
```

Item fields:

- `module`, `kind`, `key` — required identity. `kind` is one of `project`, `requirement`, `actor_role`, `object_relation`, `action_authorization`, `workflow_connector`, `acceptance`, `resource`. Identity segments are stable lowercase keys; the unique project item is always `project/project/project`.
- `status` — optional, `closed` (default) or `decision_required`; `decision_required` must match at least one unresolved decision.
- `requirement_keys`, `depends_on`, `decisions` — optional arrays (default empty). `depends_on` entries are full `module/kind/key` addresses.
- `payload` — the item body (default `{}`), identical to the Ledger item payload contract for that kind.

One `module/kind/key` may be declared exactly once across all model files. Group items by owning module — typically one file per module (`backend/model/<module>.json`). Do not add envelope fields (`contract_version`, `module`, `kind`, `key`) inside `payload`, and do not nest `status`, `requirement_keys`, `depends_on`, or `decisions` there.

## Requirement payload

A `requirement` item's `payload.requirement` carries the requirement statement plus its `behaviors[]` array of behavior-owner tuples (owner, resource_key, and the tuple fields defined in [behavior owner decision](capabilities/behavior-owner-decision.md)). An empty `behaviors` array is legal only when the payload also supplies a non-empty `no_executable_behavior_reason` string explaining why the requirement owns no executable behavior (for example, purely declarative authorization/navigation policy carried by roles, data permissions, and views). The field must be absent when `behaviors` is non-empty; `model plan` fails closed on both violations (`empty behaviors require a reason` / `ledger.requirement_incomplete`).

For `object_sql_v1`, use exactly one project-owned SQL file named after the Report key instead of embedding a large escaped SQL string. Replace only the `sql` member with `"sql_file":"backend/reports/<report-key>.sql"`. `model plan|plan|apply` requires that exact canonical project-relative regular file, rejects symlinks/traversal and simultaneous `sql` + `sql_file`, normalizes line endings and a final newline, records its SHA-256 in the apply receipt, and embeds the normalized SQL into the existing published Runtime contract. `sql_file` is not a Runtime field or a query DSL; Runtime still receives `object_sql_v1.sql`, and `migrate export-model` may therefore emit the compatible inline form.

## Commands

```text
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model check        --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model plan --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model plan     --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" apply model    --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --go-module-path <domain-qualified-module> [--environment <name> | --service <url>] [--allow-destructive] [--sync-only] [--evolution-audit-sha256 <emitted-sha256> --evolution-reason <reviewed-reason>]
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" migrate export-model   --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" [--force]
```

- `preflight` is the authoritative no-HTTP, local-read-only repair loop. It reuses the same model/SQL loader, strict item contract, Ledger graph, in-process authoring checks, deterministic Project Contract projector, and Runtime-manifest compiler as the formal path. It atomically replaces `.domainry/builder/disposable/model-preflight-result.json` for both `valid` and `repair_required`; stdout contains only `state`, `issue_count`, the project-relative artifact locator, SHA-256, and identity. A repair result exits non-zero. Read the artifact, batch-repair the reported issues, and rerun the direct command; do not implement a bespoke `jq`/regex preflight. This local boundary does not claim live Plane, Runtime configuration, provider, database, or scenario checks.
- `validate` parses every model file, enforces the item contract, and reports the pending plan counts without writing model/Ledger state.
- `plan` additionally lists the exact item IDs classified as create, update, or delete.
- `apply` is the single release command: it converges the Ledger to the model files, checks the aggregated metadata checklist, then chains live validation, signed publication, dependency resolution, backend materialization/evolution, and source finalization, stopping at the first failing stage. Every release apply resolves the dependency seed in staging before it installs files or writes a successful materialization receipt; a resolution failure stops closed and must be repaired before another round. For an existing Builder delivery change, the first run emits `evolution_review_required` plus an audit path and SHA-256. Inspect the immutable audit and rerun the same product command with that exact emitted SHA-256 and a concrete review reason; never calculate or substitute the hash. After any other failure, repair the model files or reported stage input before rerunning the direct command. stdout carries one compact summary; the complete receipt is written to `.domainry/builder/model-apply.json`. `--sync-only` stops after the Ledger sync and checklist for local iteration without a Domainry Plane target.
- `export` bootstraps model files from the current Ledger (one file per module) for a project created before this workflow; it refuses to overwrite existing model files without `--force`.

CAS identities, batch contexts, and Ledger journals are handled entirely inside the CLI. Never compute, copy, or supply a SHA-256 by hand, and never call Domainry Plane directly or reconstruct its request signing.

## Convergence and safety rules

`plan`/`apply` classify every declared item against the current Ledger:

- **create / update** — applied automatically and atomically; an unchanged item is never rewritten.
- **delete** — an item present in the Ledger but absent from the model is destructive. `apply` refuses and names the missing items until the model restores them or the run explicitly passes `--allow-destructive`.
- A **rename** of `module`, `kind`, or `key` is a delete plus a create. Treat renames as destructive: confirm data expectations first, then apply with explicit consent.
- The model owns definitions only. Runtime instance data — business records, sessions, credentials, user-role assignments made at runtime — is never compared or mutated by convergence.

Complete each module's full inventory (Objects, Relations, Actions, Roles, authorization, data scopes, Workflows, state machines, Reports, Schedulers, Automations, Connectors, seeds, acceptance) before the first `model plan`; do not validate a partial inventory and do not use `validate` or `apply` as a resource-by-resource schema probe. Immediately before the first validation, perform one cross-resource preflight over the whole draft: ownership closes **both ways** (every requirement behavior resolves to its resource, and every emitted Action/Workflow/Scheduler/Automation — including export/audit helper Actions — has one matching behavior owner); every Action's allowed roles have the required object access plus reads of every declared project relation target; Identity bootstrap/demo-user/profile references resolve; every frontend entrypoint object exists; Report SQL paths equal `backend/reports/<report-key>.sql`; export controls resolve their Report, Action, audit/download Objects, mappings, and one role's complete grant chain; every declared Object has a valid seed; and acceptance actors, roles, operations, positive cases, and denial cases resolve. Run validation only after this inventory is closed. On failure, collect and repair the complete diagnostic set and re-run once; do not revalidate after each local edit. Once validation returns `state:"valid"`, keep that model immutable while attaching evidence. Any requirement-backed edit invalidates the result and starts a new atomic `validate` + `plan` cycle. After a failed apply, fix the complete finding set in the files and re-run once.

**Initial/default-state closure is part of that single preflight.** For every explicit requirement or accepted evidence statement that names an initial or default field value, author the value as the owning `objects[].fields[].default_value`. This is mandatory when the Object is exposed through generic Runtime create (including `entrypoints[].create_objects` or a role's `<object>.create` permission); acceptance prose, a seed, a frontend form default, or an Action input constant is not metadata default behavior. Mechanically verify that every select default matches its stable field option vocabulary and every state-field default matches both that vocabulary and the owning `state_machines[].states`. If the requirement does not identify an initial/default value, do not invent one merely to satisfy prose; record only the deterministic behavior the accepted demand actually establishes.

Before that first validation, apply this strict nested-shape card; these objects reject aliases and convenient prose fields:

- `identity_bootstrap.menus[]` uses `id`, `key`, `label`, optional `description`/`route`/`icon`/`parent_id`, and required `sort_order` plus `status`; there is no `surface`. Bind roles with one row per pair, `role_menus:[{"role_id":"technician","menu_id":"menu_my_work"}]`, or with `role_menu_sets:[{"role_id":"technician","menu_ids":["menu_my_work"]}]`; never use `role_key`, `menu_keys`, or a grouped object under `role_menus`.
- Object field `validation` uses the exact Blueprint keys `min_length`, `max_length`, `min`, `max`, `pattern`, `options`, and `target`; `minimum`/`maximum` are Runtime authoring API names, not Blueprint JSON fields.
- Every `expected_reports[].metrics` value is an array; use `[]` when the scenario asserts execution/export but no metric values. It is never an object map.
- A Report emission repeats its identity inside the value: `{"collection":"reports","key":"part_usage_report","value":{"key":"part_usage_report",...}}`. The envelope `key` does not populate `value.key`; omitting the inner key makes `sql_file` resolve against an empty report key. The two keys must be identical.
- For `object_sql_v1`, each SQL `JOIN ... AS <alias>` has exactly one `join_cardinalities` entry shaped `{"alias":"<alias>","cardinality":"many_to_one"}` (or another truthful supported cardinality). It has only `alias` and `cardinality`; never use `left_alias`/`right_alias` there. Those names belong to Dataset join definitions, not Object SQL cardinality declarations.
- `report_export_controls[]` is closed to the fields listed in [reports](capabilities/reports.md). Do not invent requester/scope convenience properties; requester scoping is enforced by the declared grant chain and record mapping.
- `object_sql_v1` SQL has explicit `ORDER BY` and a literal business-bounded `LIMIT` in the inclusive range `1..10000`; the Blueprint `limit` diagnostic refers to SQL text, not a JSON `limit` property. Never use a larger placeholder such as `LIMIT 100000`.

Business menu definitions and role-menu assignments are **not emitted collections**. They are deterministic project bootstrap facts under the single project-level `identity_bootstrap` object. When acceptance names `effective_menu_list`, declare the needed `identity_bootstrap.menus` and either `role_menus` or `role_menu_sets` before apply; authoring rejects a probed role with no binding. Do not postpone that acceptance prerequisite to a manual post-apply step. Runtime's Identity menu management API remains the supported path for later operational edits; updates keep their normal schema-hash CAS contract.

`identity_bootstrap` (departments, organization scopes/memberships, workforce profiles/assignments, menus and role-menu bindings) is **not** an emits collection — an emitted collection always renders as an array and fails `schema.type: expected object`. It is a single project-level Blueprint property: declare it inside the **project item's `payload.blueprint.identity_bootstrap`** as `{"version":"1","departments":[{"id":"east","name":"East"}],"menus":[{"id":"menu_my_work","key":"my_work","label":"My work","route":"business.my_work","sort_order":10,"status":"active"}],"role_menus":[{"role_id":"technician","menu_id":"menu_my_work"}]}`. `version` is the **string** constant `"1"` (integer `1` fails `schema.const`). `demo_users[].department_id` must reference a department `id` declared there (`identity.user_department_not_found` otherwise).

`demo_users[].profile_bindings` is the single owner of a demo user's business-profile link. Its referenced profile seed must leave the profile extension's `identity_relation_field` absent; do not also write a user ID into that seed field. `model plan` rejects the two-owner form as `identity.user_profile_seed_relation_owned_twice`, before Runtime bootstrap. Runtime still converges the exact pre-existing same-user link idempotently for older valid deliveries, but a different-user replacement remains a conflict.

Two more Action/role rules the validator enforces:

- **Every project-owned Handler Action — including scheduler-driven bulk handlers — must declare at least one required payload field in `idempotency_keys`** (`ledger.action_idempotency_required`). A scheduled job's invocation payload carries the key (e.g. a required `run_date` bound from the trigger event).
- **Multiple `data_permissions[]` entries for the same object do NOT merge**: the validator reads one entry's `read`/`write` per object, so "read=department + write=own" cannot be expressed as two entries (`ledger.action_role_data_permission_required` reports the losing entry's booleans). Declare a single entry with the union capability and enforce the narrower write constraint through a before-update automation assert on the owner, a Handler precondition, or CRUD permission removal.

## Single ownership

Every rendered resource key has exactly one originating model item. A `ledger.resource_duplicate` diagnostic means a second item attempted to emit an existing resource; it is never an overlay or merge mechanism. Repair it in the model files: remove the duplicate declaration and extend the item that already owns the resource. For example, a missing permission on an emitted role belongs in the item that already emits the role, not in a new `actor_role` item emitting the same role key.

Every behavior `resource_key` must resolve to the concrete resource owned by that behavior; the exact owner-to-emitted-collection mapping and resource-key rules live in [behavior owner decision](capabilities/behavior-owner-decision.md) — do not guess a collection from prose.

Agent metadata is resource-owned in the same model: emit `skills`, `agents`, `agent_tasks`, `agent_service_principals`, and `agent_entrypoints` from separate `resource` items in dependency order, each linked to the requirement it satisfies. Never place these collections inside the project item. Read [Agents and Agent Tasks](capabilities/agents-and-agent-tasks.md) before authoring them; exact fields and references come from the live Blueprint Definition consumed by `model plan|plan|apply`.

## Action declarations

An emitted `actions[]` entry requires `key`, `name`, `object_key`, `kind`, and `audit_event`. `kind` is the closed enum `bulk_operation`, `conditional_update`, `object_create`, `object_operation`, `record_delete`, `record_operation`, `record_restore`, `record_update`, or `transition_state`.

**Kind selection for Handler Actions**: a project-owned Handler must NOT use kind `object_create` — that kind carries the system `record.create` owner, and an Action with both a system operation and a business handler owner is rejected at **Runtime bootstrap** ("action has both system operation record.create and business handler owners"); no static stage (validate/finalize/check/verify/package) catches it. Use **`object_operation`** for an object-level Handler command (creation included) and **`record_operation`** for a record-targeted one; a Handler that creates records does the create through its data capabilities.

Authorization splits by ownership and both halves are enforced at compile time (`ledger.runtime_manifest_invalid`):

- A **project-owned Handler Action** (one that declares `handler`) uses the `authorization` block (`allowed_roles`, …).
- A **system Action** (`transition_state` and every other non-Handler kind) must instead declare `permission` — it compiles to Runtime `requires_permission`. `authorization` is rejected on a system Action, and a missing `permission` is rejected too. Runtime executes a system Action for any role holding that permission, so a role that must not execute a guarded transition (for example, "only managers close") must not hold the declared permission — or the transition must be owned by a manager-only Handler Action instead.
- **The `permission` key must be exactly two dot-segments: `<object_key>.<suffix>`** (e.g. `ticket.transition_close`, not `ticket.transition.close`). Runtime authorization re-derives the check as `<action.object_key>.<last-segment>`, so a three-segment key like `ticket.transition.start` passes `model plan` and one authorization layer but is re-read as the never-granted `ticket.start` by the second — every legitimate caller then fails with 403 `backend.permission.denied` at runtime. Platform permission keys granted verbatim in `roles[].permissions` (e.g. `identity.audit.view`) are exact-match strings and are not subject to this rule; it binds project-declared Action `permission` values and object CRUD keys.

Acceptance scenarios are strict Blueprint resources, not free-form test notes. Use only the declared top-level fields `key`, `name`, `description`, `actor`, `role`, `role_key`, `seed_data`, `seed_records`, `actions`, `attempted_actions`, `workflows`, `expected_outcome`, `expected_error_code`, `expected_records`, `expected_reports`, `assertions`, and `config`; never invent shortcuts such as `objects` or `attempted_objects`. Express record/RLS expectations through `expected_records` or typed `assertions`.

`workflows` means a positive **manual** Workflow invocation and therefore requires `trigger_contract.type:"manual"`. Do not list `scheduled`, `action_completed`, or `record_event` Workflows there: the finalizer attributes them to their real trigger owner (the matching `scheduled_jobs`, Action, or Automation operation) and rejects a fabricated manual-run case with `acceptance.workflow_manual_trigger_required`.

The scenario-level `expected_outcome` closed enum is `""`, `positive`, `exception`, or `denied` — nothing else. Use `positive` for an expected success, `denied` for an expected Runtime authorization denial, and `exception` for every other expected non-success (state-machine rejection, RLS concealment, business precondition failure). Do not confuse it with the different `config.runtime_operations[].expected_outcome` enum documented below; the two enums are validated independently and values are not interchangeable. A `denied` scenario's role must actually be unable to execute every attempted Action: the composer rejects a denied scenario whose role holds the Action's authorization (`compose.acceptance_denied_role_can_execute_action`) — pick a genuinely unauthorized role or remove the grant.

### Acceptance composition rules enforced by `verify acceptance prepare`

The denominator builder enforces these composition rules; authoring scenarios without them costs one repair round each:

- **Requirement coverage**: every `requirement` item — including purely declarative ones such as acceptance provisioning or navigation — must be reachable from at least one `acceptance` item's `requirement_keys` whose scenarios produce executable cases (`acceptance.requirement_coverage_missing: <key> resources=N operations=0 cases=0` otherwise). Cases come only from `actions`/`attempted_actions`, `workflows`, `expected_reports`, and `config.runtime_operations`; a scenario carrying only `expected_records` produces no case.
- **Write denial coverage**: every write operation — each write Action and each write `runtime_operations` route — needs a denied-role case (`acceptance.permission_denial_missing`). For Actions, author a `denied` scenario with an unauthorized role. For typed routes, author a scenario whose `runtime_operations` entry sets **`"case": "permission_denied"`** (setting only `expected_outcome: denied` is not recognized); its default error code is `auth.permission_denied`, and its role must genuinely lack the route's required permissions.
- **Handler positive coverage is symmetric and DIRECT**: every Handler Action also needs a positive scenario whose `actions` list references it directly with an allowed role (`ledger.action_positive_scenario_missing`). Coverage through a Workflow branch that invokes the Handler does not count — a scheduler-driven or approval-driven Handler still needs one direct positive probe (e.g. the operator role invoking it with an explicit payload).
- **Every declared Object needs at least one seed** — including runtime-product objects such as reminder records or export audit/download artifacts (`ledger.seed_evidence_incomplete` names the missing objects); there is no exemption for objects normally populated only at runtime.
- Treat seed records as a closed typed graph before apply: every required field needs a value or declared default, every `$record:<seed-key>` relation must target a seed of the relation's declared object, option values must belong to the field value domain, and undeclared fields are errors. `model plan` reports these at the exact seed field; do not defer them to Runtime bootstrap.
- **Relation-typed `payload_fields` require `target_object_key`** referencing a **project** object; a Foundation target (e.g. an organization unit) is not resolvable there — pass the identifier as `text` and keep the Object field itself as the real relation.
- **Denied report cases are auto-derived — never author them.** A scenario referencing a report in `expected_reports` must use a role that IS allowed to read it (`acceptance.report_role_not_allowed` otherwise). For a protected report (non-empty `audience_roles`/`required_permissions`), the builder automatically finds an unauthorized role and emits the `permission_denied` case itself; it fails `acceptance.report_denied_role_missing` if no declared role is unauthorized. The same auto-derivation applies to Workflow denied cases.
- **CRUD/list/navigation coverage uses `config.runtime_operations` route keys** from the pinned Runtime Domain API `routes` map. The most-used keys: `object_query` (bounded list GET /objects/{objectKey}/records), `object_detail`, `object_create` (idempotency-key required), `object_update`, `object_delete`, `object_action`, `record_action`, `record_export`, `record_import_apply`, `effective_menu_list` (GET /identity/effective-menus), `business_notification_list`/`business_notification_stream` (SSE). Verify a key's readiness through `model capability` before relying on it.
- **Prepare prerequisites**: a current verification receipt and a running healthy managed Runtime of the exact current cohort. Pass `--project` as an **absolute path** — a relative path currently fails the database-identity check with `managed Runtime database identity escapes the current project`.

Their nested shapes are closed too. `expected_records[]` accepts only `object_key`, `record_key`, `field_key`, `state`, `count`, and `values`; it has no `scope`. `expected_reports[]` accepts only `report_key`, `expected_run`, `expected_export`, `filters`, and array-valued `metrics` (use `[]`, not `{}`, when no metric is asserted). Assertions accept only their published typed assertion fields.

When a requirement consumes a typed Runtime capability that is not already represented by `actions`, `workflows`, or `expected_reports`, declare it under the scenario's `config.runtime_operations`. Each entry uses only `route_key` from the pinned Runtime Domain API plus optional `case`, `lifecycle`, `restart_sensitive`, `expected_outcome`, and `expected_error_code`; unknown fields, wrong field types, and route keys absent from the pinned Runtime Domain API fail during `model plan` (`evidence.typed_operation_route_unknown`). Use separate positive and `permission_denied` scenarios/roles for a write. The acceptance denominator resolves the route to the unified capability disclosure, preserves its real read/write effect class, required permissions, and SSE disposition, and rejects an allowed role labeled denied, a positive role missing the published permission, or a write without both positive and denied coverage. `expected_outcome`, when supplied, is one of `passed`, `denied`, `conflict`, `rejected`, `concealed`, `not_found`, or `failed`. For an SSE route, the case/lifecycle must be `sse_disconnect_resume`/`disconnect_resume` and `restart_sensitive` must be omitted or `false`: Last-Event-ID reconnect is not a managed process restart and requires only the stream transcript plus durable refetch. Do not reduce it to a connection-open check or attach unrelated restart/audit evidence.

```json
{"config": {
  "runtime_operations": [
    {"route_key":"business_notification_stream","case":"sse_disconnect_resume","lifecycle":"disconnect_resume"}
  ]
}}
```

A positive scenario's referenced seed records must already satisfy every source-owned Handler precondition needed for the expected success path. Every positive or denied role used by executable acceptance must have a project-declared `demo_users[]` identity. Bind a specific identity through `actor`; when an automatic standard case only has a role, that role must have exactly one demo user or exactly one user marked `acceptance_default:true`. The default applies across both `role_key` and `role_keys`; alphabetical order is never identity resolution. A role label alone is not a login. Keep separate negative business-precondition scenarios when that rejection matters. Denied authorization scenarios remain distinct and must fail at the Runtime authorization boundary.

When a positive Action needs a value the standard runner cannot derive, declare the runner-owned fixture in that scenario's open `config` map: `"action_payloads":[{"action_key":"<declared scenario action>","fields":{"<payload key>":{"value":<typed scalar>}}}]`. An omitted `encoding` requires a literal conforming exactly to the declared scalar payload type; relation/reference literals accept only `$record:<seed-key>` of the declared target, and user literals accept only `$actor`. The existing `{"encoding":"json","value":<array or object>}` form remains available only for `text`/`long_text`, resolving nested `$record:<seed-key>` values before canonical JSON encoding. The Action must belong to that positive scenario, actor plus Action must identify one scenario/role binding, and malformed, missing-seed, duplicate, or ambiguous fixtures fail closed; fixture fields are never conflict-mutation slots. Do not declare fixtures for values the standard type derivation already supplies.

Validation must close actor/role, object/relation, Action/authorization/data access, Automation/Workflow/Scheduler ownership, frontend entrypoints, and positive plus denied acceptance. Single-owner semantics and behavior shape tuples live in [behavior owner decision](capabilities/behavior-owner-decision.md).

## Templates

`templates/backend-model-handler-minimal/model.json.tmpl` is the directly loadable backend-model starter for a real two-object Handler transaction. Copy it to `backend/model/<module>.json`, replace only declared `{{...}}` decisions, and run `model plan`. The template is not the capability boundary: derive identity binding, custom RLS, behavior-owner paths, Surfaces, seeds, and acceptance from the routed capability documents plus bounded CLI context. Template usage and the composable `ledger-*` pattern packs are indexed in `templates/README.md`.
# Foundation capability index

Read only the documents selected here, but read all matches before authoring the Ledger. These files explain current owners; Blueprint and Runtime validators remain authoritative.

- Account, login, member/customer profile, profile binding (`identity_relation_field`, `identity_ownership`, `required_binding_key`), platform-owned profile fields: [identity/account/profile](identity-account-and-profile.md).
- Person/organization subjects, contact point, address, identifier, consent, marketing subscription, organization extension, membership, team/store/territory/warehouse scope facts: [party extensions](party-and-organization-extension.md).
- Department, organization tree, parent unit, `department_id` derivation, org-unit lifecycle: [organization units](organization-unit-and-department.md).
- Employee, manager, reporting line (`manager_id`, `manager_path`, `reporting_path`), job/position, multiple or temporary assignments: [workforce](workforce-and-reporting-line.md).
- Approval, CC, or escalation involving departments, managers, roles, or record-selected users: read organization, workforce, and the assignee-resolver decision matrix in [workflow](workflow.md) together before choosing a resolver.
- Object, field, relation, record mutation, guarded state transitions, or required lifecycle immutability: read [records](records-fields-and-relations.md), [CRUD/state machine](crud-and-state-machine.md), and [actions/transactions](actions-and-transactions.md). Prefer inline `select` values; only read the Dictionary subsection in records when one controlled vocabulary is genuinely reused and centrally localized or ordered. Reusable single-Object list/search/filter/sort semantics: [record views](record-views.md); read it with [reports](reports.md) when deciding operational records versus aggregate analytics.
- Roles, RBAC, field/reference/export policy, data scope, actor claims, RLS predicate: [permissions](permissions-and-data-scope.md). Standard role/scope/claim pairings for member portal, staff back office, multi-store: [RBAC cookbook](rbac-and-data-scope-cookbook.md).
- Behavior `owner` choice (`runtime_crud`, `business_handler`, `workflow`, `scheduler`, `automation_before`/`automation_after`), owner-to-collection mapping, `resource_key` resolution: [behavior owner decision](behavior-owner-decision.md).
- Event rules, before/after transaction boundaries, instruction selection, and automation idempotency: [automation](automation.md). Timed work: [scheduler](scheduler.md). Object analytics/export: [reports](reports.md). Business audit-event export: [permissions](permissions-and-data-scope.md) together with [backend Runtime integration](../backend-runtime.md); it is a separate Runtime report source.
- Model reasoning, structured analysis, durable AI tasks, approval-gated proposals, Workflow Agent nodes, global assistant entrypoints, service execution identity, Tool Gateway authorization, retry/cancel/recovery: [Agents and Agent Tasks](agents-and-agent-tasks.md). Read it with [workflow](workflow.md) for an `agent_task` node, [actions](actions-and-transactions.md) for proposed or allowed effects, and [reports](reports.md) for governed analytics.
- Personal Inbox, unread badge, actionable station messages, notification preferences, and the boundary between user-impacting events and operational errors: [in-app notifications](in-app-notifications.md). Read it with [backend Runtime integration](../backend-runtime.md) whenever Business Workspace or Consumer Portal requirements include a notification center.
- External effects, provider/operation discovery, connection binding, connector capability gap: [connectors](connectors.md).
- Business frontend (employee/operator UI) or customer/member frontend, navigation matrix, Portal login: [Product Surfaces](product-surfaces.md); a Runtime View is query metadata, never a frontend page.
- Backend-model starter template and composable Ledger patterns: `templates/README.md`.
## Task profile minimum reading sets

Read [development-guide](../development-guide.md) for every whole-project task, then pick exactly one profile. The routing rules above still select capability documents for the active business area.

- New project delivery: this index, routed capability documents, [domainry-plane](../domainry-plane.md), [project-mutation](../project-mutation.md), [backend-model](../backend-model.md), [authorization](../authorization.md), and [backend Runtime integration](../backend-runtime.md).
- Existing project increment: this index restricted to changed capability areas, [domainry-plane](../domainry-plane.md), [project-mutation](../project-mutation.md), and [backend-model](../backend-model.md) only when metadata changes.
- Handler-only repair: [project-mutation](../project-mutation.md), [ownership-and-extensions](../ownership-and-extensions.md), [behavior owner decision](behavior-owner-decision.md), and bounded `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" apply action-context --projection coding`; load Ledger documents only when the published contract changes.

Do not use raw `curl`, `jq`, or repository search merely to rediscover these foundation facts. Use bounded formal contract commands when an exact release-bound symbol is needed.

# Project development guide

The complete workflow is `requirements → model → apply → verify → done`. These are the only stages. Domain truth belongs to requirements; backend source implementation belongs to apply.

Use one TODO at `.domainry/development/<session-id>.md`. Its `Current stage` is the progress marker. There is no separate workflow ledger, receipt attachment list, reconciliation command, resume profile, or transition command. When a direct CLI command fails, stay in the current stage, repair the responsible project input, and rerun it.

Use only the CLI embedded in the loaded Skill:

```sh
SKILL_ROOT=<directory containing the loaded SKILL.md>
DOMAINRY_CLI="$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-cli"
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" version --json
```

Never resolve a Builder CLI through `PATH`, mix Skill installations, or call Domainry Plane as an authoring shortcut.

## requirements

Read `references/requirements-and-domain-truth.md` and `assets/BACKEND_REQUIREMENTS_PRD.template.md`. This is the single stage for both requirements discovery and domain truth.

Inspect `frontend/**` only when frontend source exists. It is evidence and remains read-only. Trace backend-dependent surfaces to exact source paths, but never make the frontend implementation the authority for missing business rules. When no frontend exists, use the caller's actual requirement authority and record that fact.

Settle, as applicable:

- identity, actors, roles, permissions, workspace and data scope;
- objects, identifiers, relations, lifecycle state, invariants and retention;
- actions, transactions, rollback, concurrency and idempotency;
- calculations, units, precision, rounding, settlement, history and corrections;
- reports, filters, sorting, stable pagination, export and totals;
- schedules, automation, notifications, files and integrations;
- success, denied, invalid, conflict, retry, restart and terminal outcomes.

Every accepted requirement needs a stable requirement ID, source, owner, acceptance result and traceability row. A business blocker exists only when an unresolved choice changes an observable result, authorization allow/deny, amount or unit semantics, irreversible external effect, or business-state flow. Do not advance until those blockers are resolved or the affected requirement is explicitly out of scope.

The output is `docs/backend-requirements-prd.md`. Platform capabilities do not decide domain facts.

## model

Read `references/backend-model.md`, then `references/capabilities/README.md`. Load only capability references required by the accepted PRD. Map settled behavior to declarative project-owned `backend/model/*.json` and referenced `backend/reports/*.sql`.

Bounded discovery and validation commands are:

```sh
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model capabilities --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model capability --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --key <category>
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model check --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model plan --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
```

Do not load every capability reference. Do not use capability availability to weaken or invent requirements. Review plan output for removals, incompatible changes, and required evolution decisions before advancing.

## apply

Read `references/project-mutation.md`. Apply the reviewed declarative model with the only normal release command:

```sh
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" apply model --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" \
  --go-module-path <domain-qualified-module> --product-surfaces <reviewed-surfaces>
```

Then read `references/ownership-and-extensions.md` and implement the project-owned source required by the applied model. Generated source, manifests, delivery receipts, caches, journals and managed Runtime state are not authoring surfaces.

Use focused context only for the item being implemented:

```sh
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" apply action-context --projection coding --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" <action-key>
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" apply connector-context --projection coding --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" <connector-key>
```

One user intent that changes business state must remain one governed command. Preserve the accepted transaction boundary, rollback, authorization, data scope, idempotency fingerprint, exact calculation semantics, audit/outbox correlation and external-effect terminal state. Do not add placeholders or silent success handlers.

Run focused tests while iterating, then:

```sh
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" apply prepare --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" apply finalize --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
```

Implement the complete project business-flow test harness and every applicable
large fixture script in this stage, then run their focused tests. Advance only
after source finalization and the affected backend test set pass. `verify` is
execution and evidence capture, not the first authoring location for a whole
test suite.

## verify

Read `references/evidence-levels.md`, `references/verification.md`, `references/production-verification-checklist.md`, and `references/backend-runtime.md`.

Run structural verification and packaging independently:

```sh
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" verify structure --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" verify package --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
```

Start exactly one managed Runtime from the current package on a dedicated numeric loopback address, inspect it, exercise the accepted scenarios, then stop it when finished:

```sh
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" verify runtime start --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --address 127.0.0.1:<port>
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" verify runtime status --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" verify runtime stop --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
```

Structural success does not prove real behavior. Verification covers the changed operation denominator and applicable positive, denied, scoped, invalid, conflict, rollback, concurrency, idempotency, persistence, restart, worker, report, pagination, export and provider-terminal outcomes. Bind observations to the current model, source, package, Runtime and database cohort. Treat Runtime identifiers and principal context as opaque values returned by formal APIs.

Run the selected highest-risk semantic canary first. Only after its strict positive or denied/conflict oracle passes should broader Runtime scenario integration proceed. A structural pass never upgrades delivery evidence into observed real-data behavior.

Frontend build and visual validation are outside this Skill. Record frontend-owned mismatches as findings with exact evidence; do not hide them with a backend workaround.

## done

Resolve all in-scope findings, set `Current stage: done`, and run:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-todo-check.py" \
  --todo "$PROJECT_ROOT/.domainry/development/$SESSION_ID.md" --expected-stage done
```

The final report names the delivery identity, changed files, tests, managed Runtime result, highest evidence level and explicit non-blocking limitations. It does not claim behavior that was not observed.
# Domainry Plane boundary

V2 uses Domainry Plane only through the single packaged `domainry-cli` executable.

Choose one explicit `--environment <local|dev|stage|online>` or `--service <url>` target for `apply model` and Connector definition discovery. Keep that target fixed for the batch.

Release only with:

```text
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" apply model --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --go-module-path <domain-qualified-module> --product-surfaces <reviewed-surfaces> [one target]
```

The command converges `backend/model/*.json`, checks the complete model, validates it with Domainry Plane, publishes the immutable delivery, and materializes or evolves the backend. Source preparation, implementation, tests, and `apply finalize` follow explicitly in the same apply stage. For an existing Builder delivery change, inspect the first run's immutable evolution audit, then rerun the same product command with `--evolution-audit-sha256 <emitted-sha256> --evolution-reason <reviewed-reason>`. A stale audit fails closed. Repair any other failed input or stage before rerunning the direct command.

Do not call Domainry Plane directly, reconstruct signing, hand-edit delivery state, or invent separate validate/publish/materialize commands. The current Builder flow keeps reviewed evolution inside `apply model`; it exposes no neighboring delivery-maintenance command surface.
# Authorization and behavior ownership

Keep Action invocation, object permission, data scope, field policy, Surface access, assurance, and execution ownership separate.

- Give every Handler Action exactly one execution owner and exact `allowed_roles`.
- Use `object_operation` when no existing record ID is supplied; use `record_operation` only for a caller-supplied existing record.
- Declare every `list`, `get`, `get_for_update`, `create`, `update`, `conditional_update`, delete/restore, and Connector capability used by the algorithm. Locking is not mutation authority.
- Put volatile correctness invariants in generated conditional mutation and preserve its typed conflict error when required. Do not replace concurrency semantics with a friendly precheck.
- Grant relation-target reads and narrow data scope explicitly. A display reference permission is not target read permission.
- Keep direct CRUD permission separate from Handler EffectAuthority. Never widen a business role merely to collect audit evidence.
- Before the single live validation, compute Handler EffectAuthority for every `(Action, allowed_role, data_access)` tuple. Every allowed role needs a non-empty data scope on each referenced Object, with `read: true` for `get`, `get_for_update`, `optional`, `list`, `exists`, or `count`, and `write: true` for `create`, `update`, `conditional_update`, `delete`, or `restore`. The role does not need direct CRUD permission merely because the Handler holds EffectAuthority, but missing data scope still fails compilation.
- Validate that complete matrix once across all Handlers; do not wait for live validation to reveal one missing role/Object grant at a time. Narrow `allowed_roles` only when the PRD actor truly must not execute the Action, never as a shortcut around EffectAuthority.
- After backend implementation and real Runtime/database data acceptance, count every published Action and persist TODO matrix rows with delta scope: for a full batch, one row per published Action with total Actions equal to matrix rows; for an existing-project increment, one row per Action added or changed in this batch plus summary rows that reference the prior accepted matrix evidence for unchanged Actions, with authored plus referenced rows still covering the published total. When a light batch changes no Action, role, permission, scope, or menu, omit this acceptance from the instantiated TODO with the omission recorded in the header, or close it as not applicable with scope evidence referencing the prior accepted matrices and totals instead of re-authoring rows. Record target, permission or exact `allowed_roles`, data scope, allowed and denied probes, current Runtime/persistence evidence, and result. Zero unowned or untested Actions is the backend completion condition.
- Treat Action creation and its Role authorization as one modeling change. Before moving to the next Action, add its truthful `authorization.allowed_roles`, the matching scoped `data_permissions` for every Handler access and declared project relation target, and positive/denied acceptance actors. Checklist aggregates `compose.action_role_authorization_missing`, `compose.action_role_data_permission_missing`, and `compose.action_role_relation_target_read_missing`; repair the full Action/Role/Object set together. For non-Handler Actions, at least one declared role must hold the published `permission`; Handler grant derivation is owned by [actions-and-transactions](capabilities/actions-and-transactions.md).
- Model one positive allowed scenario, role-denied scenario, and when relevant sibling/out-of-scope concealed scenario.
- Every entrypoint object list requires the bound role's matching object permission plus a compatible data permission — closure rule owned by [permissions-and-data-scope](capabilities/permissions-and-data-scope.md); an entrypoint list is not an implicit grant.
- Treat Runtime-derived organization claims and Product Surface identity as trusted Runtime facts, never request input or guessed headers.
- `roles[].data_permissions[]` is a closed policy object with explicit `read`/`write` booleans — full field contract in [permissions-and-data-scope](capabilities/permissions-and-data-scope.md).
- Sensitive fields are fail-closed; the exact `field_permissions` contract and live-value proof requirements live in [permissions-and-data-scope](capabilities/permissions-and-data-scope.md).
- Treat menu assignment as persisted authorization-adjacent evidence, not UI configuration. For every application role, the Agent uses a project-provisioned non-human acceptance identity and real Runtime session to compare actual database menu definitions and role-menu assignments with `GET /identity/effective-menus?surface=business_workspace`, then matches every effective route to the frontend Route Registry. Never ask the user to log in, switch roles, repeat login, or provide personal credentials for acceptance. Record the role-effective-menu and menu-route matrices in the current TODO; Blueprint or Mock declarations are not database proof.

Use the exact project-managed packet path returned by `apply prepare` for delivered-batch Handler contracts, typed APIs, enum values, scaffold/import rules, error semantics, and bounded evidence. Inspect the envelope's small Action index first; then use local `jq` to select exactly one Action by `action_key` and only its needed document content by document SHA. Never `cat` or print the whole packet, never use `latest.json`, and never repeat `apply action-context --projection coding` across the same installed batch. Use focused `apply action-context` only for an isolated repair or an audit-bound pending evolution outside that packet. Do not read generated capabilities or context files directly.

If Definition/compiler/Runtime cannot express a required role, scope, assurance, atomicity, or effect, record a platform owner gap; do not move the policy into UI or an unrelated Handler.
# Backend Runtime integration and managed proof

This reference covers the closed Runtime HTTP boundary, Action invocation, managed Runtime proof, and backend Handler coding idioms. Capability discovery comes from the CLI-compiled authority contract; frontend dependency installation and package wiring are outside this Skill.

## Closed HTTP boundary

Project-owned backend source must not add, register, proxy, or require any application-facing HTTP interface. Do not create a project-local HTTP handler, router, controller, middleware endpoint, BFF, API proxy, serverless function, or alternate transport route. Application-facing client selection and wiring belong to the frontend owner outside this Skill; Builder models only the Application Delivery-published `runtime-domain-api-v1` contract.

Custom source-owned Action Handlers expose no separate HTTP route; Runtime invokes them only through the published object or record Action operations below. Connector providers may perform contract-declared outbound calls through generated Connector APIs and governed transport, but they must not publish an inbound project API. If the published Runtime CRUD, Action, Report, file, authentication, or Connector contracts cannot express a required behavior, record the exact platform-owner finding and repair that owner in the same session instead of adding an HTTP endpoint; only the terminal policy's proved unrecoverable conditions permit stopping.

## Action invocation

Select object versus record invocation from the Runtime-published Action `kind`, using `runtimeActionInvocationScope`; never infer it from UI layout or from whether the execution owner is a custom Handler.

- `object_create`, `object_operation`, and `bulk_operation` use `runObjectAction` at `POST /objects/{objectKey}/actions/{actionKey}/run`.
- `record_update`, `record_delete`, `record_restore`, `transition_state`, `conditional_update`, and `record_operation` use `runRecordAction` at `POST /objects/{objectKey}/records/{recordID}/actions/{actionKey}`.

Backend acceptance wraps typed Action input as `{"data": <payload>}`; a bare payload is invalid for the Action invocation contract.

Call `listActions(objectKey)` first and pass the returned full `action_definition.key` unchanged to `runObjectAction` or `runRecordAction`; never shorten `group_class.book_group_class` to `book_group_class`. Use the exact storage values published by the Action input contract, such as `member`, not translated labels such as `会员`. A `record_operation` also requires the existing record ID in the record route; the presence of a button on an object list does not turn it into an object Action.

Frontends never call a generated Handler directly. Preserve the bounded Action input/output contract, workspace, Product Surface, bearer identity, request ID, idempotency key, assurance token, and concurrency value. Preserve Runtime result references and triggered workflows instead of reducing the response to a success boolean.

One accepted business intent must produce one Runtime mutation request (verification check G04). For example, “open table” is one declared Action call, not `create table session` followed by separate status, occupancy, audit, and notification mutations. Do not use `Promise.all`, sequential mutation hooks, retries with new keys, or a browser-side rollback to assemble one atomic backend command. Put the complete typed input on the Action and let its Runtime-owned unit of work perform all effects. Refetch/invalidation after the response and polling a returned job are allowed reads; they must not hide additional writes.

## Managed Runtime proof

Start and inspect the Runtime directly with the packaged CLI and an explicit numeric loopback address such as `127.0.0.1:<dedicated-port>`. Use `verify runtime start`, then `verify runtime status`. If either command fails, remain in `verify`, diagnose the owner, repair it, and rerun the direct command. Stop with `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" verify runtime stop --project <project>` after acceptance. The managed receipt records the address, so subsequent acceptance commands use the same Runtime cohort. Never background-launch, discover arbitrary PIDs, kill unrelated processes, or start a second managed Runtime for the same project.

Runtime proof must cover declared allowed, denied, and scoped actors; Action effects; conditional conflicts; transaction rollback; idempotent replay without a second mutation or receipt; workflows/outbox; durable audit; and current delivery/package/Runtime receipt identity. Use task-published database evidence paths; do not rediscover private schema.

Stop Runtime and reclaim ports and processes after scenarios. A running process, local HTTP response, or browser screenshot without matching delivery, package, and Runtime identity is not release evidence.

## Handler coding idioms (validated against the live Runtime)

These idioms come from real Handler defects observed at runtime; `apply finalize`, compile, and tests do NOT catch any of them.

**Finalizer source-contract preflight.** Unlike the idioms below, `apply finalize` DOES reject the following three contracts (`backend_technical_contract` check), so each violation costs a failed-finalize round-trip — one real run hit 8 violations at once. Check every Handler before finalizing: (1) no generated capability I/O inside any loop (`for`/`range`) or recursive call cycle — do pure selection into bounded slices and call the generated batch/query capability once outside the loop; (2) every List query declares `Page(page, pageSize)` with a literal page size from 1 through 200 — an unpaged first result is forbidden; (3) no discarded call result or error — assign every capability return and handle every error. Generated batch inputs are 1 through 200, ordered one-to-one, and inherit the Action Workspace, Principal, grants, Scope, and transaction. Minimal accepted fan-out shape:

```go
// Pure selection: capability I/O only outside loops.
orders, err := caps.RepairOrder.List(ctx, data.NewRepairOrderQuery().
    WhereStatusEqual(schema.RepairOrderStatusDispatched).
    OrderByIDAscending().
    Page(1, 200)) // literal page size, 1..200
if err != nil {
    return out, err
}
pending := make([]schema.RepairOrder, 0, runCapacity)
for _, order := range orders { // pure filtering loop: no capability calls here
    if len(pending) == runCapacity {
        break
    }
    if eligible(order) {
        pending = append(pending, order)
    }
}
queries := make([]data.DispatchReceiptQuery, len(pending))
for index, order := range pending { // pure request construction only
    queries[index] = data.NewDispatchReceiptQuery().
        WhereOrderIDEqual(order.ID).
        WhereBusinessDateEqual(businessDate)
}
exists, err := caps.DispatchReceipt.ExistsBatch(ctx, queries) // one call, outside loops
if err != nil {
    return out, err
}
// Build CreateBatch and notification DispatchBatch inputs in pure loops, then
// invoke each batch once outside loops and return every error unchanged.
```

**Build tag.** Backend compile requires the Domain SDK build constraint: a plain `go build ./...` fails on `verifiedDomainSDKBuildConstraint`. The tag is published as `schema.DomainSDKBuildConstraint` in the generated schema package's revision constants; run all backend commands as `go build|vet|test -tags "$(go run ./cmd/... 2>/dev/null || grep -roh 'domainry_domain_sdk_[a-f0-9]*' backend/generated/ | head -1)" ./...` — or read the constant from `backend/generated/schema/revision.gen.go`. The CLI's own `verify structure` supplies the tag automatically; only manual Go commands need it.

**ConditionalUpdate requires a real condition.** A `conditional_update` Handler mutation without a compare-and-set token or predicate fails at runtime with `backend.generated.conditional_mutation_required`. Attach the condition observed under `GetForUpdate`:

```go
mutation := data.NewTicketUpdate(ticket.ID).SetAssigneeID(assignee)
if ticket.AssigneeID == nil {
    mutation = mutation.RequireAssigneeIDNull("ticket.assign.conflict")
} else {
    mutation = mutation.RequireAssigneeIDEqual(*ticket.AssigneeID, "ticket.assign.conflict")
}
updated, err := caps.Ticket.ConditionalUpdate(ctx, mutation)
```

`Require<Field>Equal/NotEqual/Null(errorCode)` predicates and `WithExpectedUpdatedAt(...)` are the generated condition surface (arithmetic `Increment*`/`Decrement*` effects are inherently compare-and-set and also satisfy the requirement). On idempotent replay the predicate legitimately differs (equal-to-current instead of null); test assertions must compare per-execution expected mutations, not demand identical mutations.

The generated data package exports `ValidateConditionalMutation`, and both the real data layer and the scaffolded fakes enforce it — a mutation with no condition fails unit tests with `backend.generated.conditional_mutation_required`. A hand-written fake must route through the same helper; never write one that accepts an unconditional mutation. As a cheap belt-and-suspenders guard for call sites no unit case exercises, after implementing each module and before `apply finalize`, run the static self-check from the project root and require exit code 0 (`grep -L` alone does not encode the verdict in its exit status, so use the wrapper below):

```bash
bash -c 'viol=$(grep -rl --include="*.go" -e ".ConditionalUpdate(" backend | grep -v "/generated/" | grep -v "_test\.go" | xargs -r grep -LE "Require[A-Za-z]+\(|WithExpectedUpdatedAt\(|Increment[A-Za-z]*\(|Decrement[A-Za-z]*\("); [ -z "$viol" ] || { echo "$viol"; exit 1; }'
```

Exit 1 lists every file that builds a `ConditionalUpdate` with no condition anywhere in that file; each will fail live with `backend.generated.conditional_mutation_required`. The check is file-granular: a file that mixes one conditioned and one bare call still passes, so keep one handler per file (the default layout). Record the direct command and result as evidence in the `apply` section of the development TODO.

**NotificationIntent.SubjectVersion must be non-empty.** `runtimeext.NotificationIntent` fails `backend.notification.action_intent_invalid` when `SubjectVersion` is empty. Generated typed reads and mutation results expose `UpdatedAt`; mutation results receive it from the same canonical staged commit that Runtime persists. Use the subject record's `UpdatedAt` (including the value returned by `ConditionalUpdate`) as `SubjectVersion`; do not substitute transport metadata such as `request_id`, leave the field empty, or skip the dispatch.

**Transition Actions from Handlers or probes** must send the target state in the request payload (see `crud-and-state-machine.md`): a payload-less transition fails closed with 400 `backend.action.transition_payload_required`.
