```json
    {"key":"owner_user","name":"Owner","type":"user","required":false,"config":{"scope_owner":true,"auto_assign_current_user":true}},
    {"key":"owner_department_id","name":"Owner department ID","type":"text","required":false,"config":{}},
    {"key":"owner_department_path","name":"Owner department path","type":"text","required":false,"config":{}}
  ]}],
  "identity_bootstrap":{
    "version":"1",
    "departments":[{"id":"operations","name":"Operations","status":"active"}],
    "workforce_profiles":[{"id":"operator_workforce","organization_id":"default","identity_user_id":"operator_user","worker_no":"W-001","worker_type":"employee","work_status":"active","primary_assignment_id":"operator_primary"}],
    "workforce_assignments":[{"id":"operator_primary","workforce_profile_id":"operator_workforce","organization_unit_id":"operations","assignment_type":"primary","status":"active"}]
  },
  "demo_users":[{"key":"operator_user","user_id":"operator_user","name":"Operator User","role_key":"operator"}],
  "permissions":[{"key":"work_item.read"},{"key":"work_item.create"}],
  "roles":[{"key":"operator","name":"Operator","record_scope":"department","permissions":["work_item.read","work_item.create"],"data_permissions":[{"object_key":"work_item","scope":"department","read":true,"write":true}]}],
  "seed_records":[{"key":"work_item_unassigned","object_key":"work_item","data":{}}]
}
```

This fragment includes the identity and permission declarations needed by the scope contract; merge it into the other required top-level Blueprint collections before whole-document validation.

An object granted `owned_records` must independently expose an owner field resolvable by Runtime: an explicit `scope_owner`, the declared identity relation of an Identity Profile Extension, or a Runtime owner/user-field fallback. An arbitrary business relation does not inherit ownership. The validator rejects `owned_records` when none of those resolvers exists.

## Handler cross-object writes are bound by the CALLER's data permissions

A Handler mutation on any object is authorized against the invoking principal's `data_permissions` — declaring the write in the Action's `handler.data_access`/EffectAuthority does NOT bypass row scope. If a role may invoke a Handler that creates or updates another object (e.g. conversion creating a `customer`), that role needs a truthful `write: true` data permission on that object (with a scope the candidate row satisfies — mind the department anchor fields above). To keep such an object "read-only" for direct use, simply do not declare its `<object>.create/update/delete` permission keys: the CRUD routes stay blocked by the missing permission while the Handler path works through the data permission.

# Behavior owner decision

## Problem and owner
Every executable behavior in a requirement Ledger item declares exactly one `owner`. The owner decides which engine executes the behavior and which emitted resource must exist. This document is the single home for the owner decision matrix and the owner-to-collection mapping; `backend-model.md` links here instead of restating it. The authoritative contract is `behaviorOwnerShapes` and the owner-collection map in `internal/builder/blueprintledger/ledger.go`; the Ledger validator, not this document, is the fact source.

## Supported model and Blueprint expression

### Decision matrix
Each owner accepts exactly one `trigger|scope|atomicity|failure_semantics` tuple (source: `behaviorOwnerShapes`, `internal/builder/blueprintledger/ledger.go`). Any other combination fails `ledger.behavior_ownership_invalid`.

| owner | trigger | scope | atomicity | failure_semantics | Choose when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `runtime_crud` | `record_write` | `single_record` | `single_record` | `reject_write` | Plain create/read/update/delete of one Object under RBAC/RLS, no cross-record command logic. |
| `runtime_system_action` | `business_command` | `single_record` | `single_record` | `rollback_command` | A named business command on one record that the platform executes (state transition style), no project code. |
| `automation_before` | `before_persistence` | `single_record` | `single_record` | `reject_write` | Declarative guard/derivation that must veto or adjust a single record before it persists. |
| `automation_after` | `after_commit` | `single_record` | `post_commit_eventual` | `preserve_committed_write` | Declarative reaction after a committed write (notify, follow-up record); must never undo the commit. |
| `business_handler` | `business_command` | `multi_record` | `multi_record` | `rollback_command` | One atomic command reads/writes multiple records or needs project code; requires a concrete capability gap. |
| `workflow` | `workflow_progression` | `process` | `long_running` | `resume_process` | Multi-step human/system process with stages, approval, resumption. |
| `scheduler` | `schedule` | `process` | `long_running` | `retry_schedule` | Time-driven recurring or delayed work with retry semantics. |

### Owner to emitted collection
Ledger owner resolution uses these exact emitted collections (source: owner-collection map in `internal/builder/blueprintledger/ledger.go`). The behavior's exact `resource_key` must appear in that collection or graph validation fails `ledger.behavior_resource_not_found`.

| owner | emitted collection |
| --- | --- |
| `runtime_crud` | `objects` |
| `runtime_system_action` | `actions` |
| `business_handler` | `actions` |
| `automation_before`, `automation_after` | `automation_rules` |
| `workflow` | `workflows` |
| `scheduler` | `scheduled_jobs` |

Do not guess aliases such as `schedulers`, `scheduler_definitions`, `automations`, or `workflow_definitions`; those never close the owner reference. Every behavior `resource_key` must resolve to the concrete resource owned by that behavior: an exact Object key for `runtime_crud`, an exact Action key for `business_handler`/`runtime_system_action`, or the exact declared Workflow/Scheduler/Automation key. Never invent umbrella keys such as `runtime.records`; split multi-Object CRUD into one behavior per Object before the first full validation.

The ownership check is bidirectional: every emitted Action, Workflow, scheduled job, and Automation must also be named by one requirement behavior with the matching owner. This includes infrastructure-looking business resources such as a report export request/audit Handler Action. A resource emitted only because another resource references it is still executable and otherwise fails `ledger.behavior_owner_mismatch`.

## Reuse, extension, and prohibitions
- Behavior fields are exact: `key`, `owner`, `resource_key`, `rationale`, `trigger`, `scope`, `atomicity`, `failure_semantics`; extras or omissions fail `ledger.behavior_ownership_invalid` (`internal/builder/blueprintledger/ledger.go`).
- `business_handler` additionally requires a concrete `capability_gap`, `involved_objects`, `read_set`, `write_set`, and `transaction_requirement` — all five present, and all but `read_set` non-empty (`read_set` may be explicitly `[]` for a create-only Handler) — otherwise `ledger.business_handler_gap_required` (`internal/builder/blueprintledger/ledger.go`).
- `read_set`/`write_set` must additionally **exactly equal** the object sets derived from the Action's `handler.data_access` declarations (`ledger.business_handler_effect_set_mismatch`). A create-only Handler whose `data_access` derives no reads declares an explicitly empty `read_set: []` — the field must still be present and well-formed (`involved_objects`/`write_set` stay non-empty). A Handler that does read (e.g. an in-transaction duplicate/idempotency precheck declared as `data_access` `["exists","create"]`) lists that object in `read_set` to match.
- Every Handler Action also requires a **denied acceptance scenario using a role that does not hold its authorization** (`ledger.action_denied_scenario_missing`). Plan role design so at least one declared role is genuinely unauthorized for each Handler Action; if every business role legitimately holds the permission, add the denied probe with a role that lacks it (for example a read-only auditor) instead of skipping the probe.
- Each executable behavior has one owner. A Handler Action's declared data access is capability, not a second execution owner.
- One originating Ledger item per rendered resource key; a second item emitting the same key fails `ledger.resource_duplicate`. Repair the originating item in the model files, never add a duplicate emitter (see `backend-model.md`).

## Examples
Correct `business_handler` behavior (multi-record atomic command):

```json
{"key": "transfer_stock", "owner": "business_handler", "resource_key": "inventory.transfer_stock", "rationale": "decrement source and increment target atomically", "trigger": "business_command", "scope": "multi_record", "atomicity": "multi_record", "failure_semantics": "rollback_command", "capability_gap": "requires one atomic command across two stock records", "involved_objects": ["stock_level"], "read_set": ["stock_level"], "write_set": ["stock_level"], "transaction_requirement": "single_transaction"}
```

Wrong: single-record update declared as `business_handler` ("convenience wrapper" is not a capability gap) fails `ledger.behavior_ownership_invalid`; declare it as `runtime_crud` with `trigger: "record_write"` and the Object key as `resource_key`.

Wrong: `owner: "scheduler"` with `resource_key: "daily_cleanup"` while the project emits no `scheduled_jobs` entry with that key fails `ledger.behavior_resource_not_found`; emit the scheduled job in its owning item first.

Wrong: `automation_after` declared with `failure_semantics: "reject_write"` fails `ledger.behavior_ownership_invalid`; after-commit reactions must declare `preserve_committed_write`, and a pre-persistence veto belongs to `automation_before`.

## Authority and limits

The owner shape tuples and the owner-to-collection map are owned by `internal/builder/blueprintledger/ledger.go`; drift tests in `internal/builder/blueprintledger/behavior_owner_doc_drift_test.go` pin this document to them. This document adds no semantics of its own.

### Typical diagnostics when the owner is wrong
- `ledger.behavior_ownership_invalid`: tuple or field set does not match the owner shape; re-decide the owner from the matrix instead of mutating one field.
- `ledger.business_handler_gap_required`: the behavior does not justify project code; either supply the concrete gap fields or downgrade to a platform owner.
- `ledger.behavior_resource_not_found`: the owning collection lacks `resource_key`; emit the resource in its originating item, do not rename the behavior.
- `ledger.resource_duplicate`: the repair was attempted in a new item instead of the originating one; delete the duplicate and CAS-update the original.
# Automation

> **TL;DR** — Owns: declarative Automation Rules, before/after transaction boundaries, instruction selection, automation idempotency. Read when: a single-record guard/derivation before persistence or a declarative reaction after commit is required. Never: use an after-commit rule to undo a committed write.

Every create trigger must close both public record-creation acceptance roles before apply: at least one role truthfully has the exact record creation permission plus write data access (or `workspace.admin`), and at least one role truthfully denies that same mutation. A permission without matching `data_permissions[].write:true` is a negative role, not a positive role. Update/delete rules may observe writes owned by a Handler, Workflow, or another Runtime capability, so their actor closure is derived from that real command owner rather than forcing a synthetic direct-CRUD grant.

## Problem and owner
Runtime automation owns before/after event rules, conditions, instructions and durable execution evidence.

## Supported model and Blueprint expression
Declare trigger phase, target object, filters/conditions and supported effects. Before rules guard or normalize; after rules perform durable follow-up through published instructions.

The exact rule shape requires `key`, `name`, `object_key`, `enabled`, object-valued `trigger`, and a non-empty `instructions` array. Put `phase` and `operation` inside `trigger`; do not author top-level `phase` or `event`. Each instruction requires `key` and `type`. Supported types are `assert`, `derive_fields`, `emit_event`, `invoke_business_action`, and `start_workflow`; `audit` is not an instruction type. Before-persistence rules may use only synchronous guard/derive semantics. After-persistence rules may invoke an Action, start a Workflow, or emit an event. `invoke_business_action` requires `config.action_key`; `start_workflow` requires `config.workflow_key`.

**Rule scope: a `before` rule fires on EVERY write path of its trigger operation** — direct CRUD, `transition_state` Actions, and Handler mutations all pass through the same before-update/before-create pipeline, and there is no exemption mechanism for Action-driven writes. Never author an automation guard that re-enforces what the state machine or Action permissions already enforce: a `before`+`update` assert on the state field blocks the sanctioned transition Actions themselves (`backend.action.assert_failed` on every transition). Illegal edges are already rejected by the state machine on all write paths; permission-guarded edges are enforced by each transition Action's `permission`. Reserve before-rules for invariants no platform owner covers.

**Deleting an automation rule from the model deactivates it on an existing managed Runtime database at the next manifest sync** — removed generated rules are disabled and stop executing after redeploy. Caveat: a rule removed and later re-added under the same identity stays disabled (sync never re-enables a disabled row); after re-adding a previously deleted rule, verify it fires and plan a fresh database cohort if it does not.

Instruction `config` contracts (`model plan` enforces these closed per-type shapes: a missing/empty required key, a key outside the contract, or an enum violation is rejected at validate time — `automation.instruction_config_key_required` / `automation.instruction_config_key_unknown` / `automation.instruction_config_value_invalid`):

- `assert` config is `{"source": <value-or-template>, "operator": <op>, "value": <value-or-template>}` — the field is named **`source`**, not `reference`/`field`. `operator` defaults to `eq`; the closed set is `eq`, `ne`, `in`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `not_empty`, `empty`, `future_date`. A failed assert blocks with `backend.action.assert_failed`.
- `derive_fields` config is `{"fields": {"<field_key>": <value-or-template>, ...}}`.
- Template values are strings with one of these prefixes, resolved against the execution context: `$payload.` / `$candidate.` (the incoming write's values), `$input.`, `$before.` (pre-image), `$record.` (the persisted record), `$actor.`, `$event.`, `$steps.`, `$actions.`. **In a `before`+`create` rule the record does not exist yet — read the incoming values with `$candidate.<field>`, not `$record.<field>`** (a `$record.` read resolves empty and an `eq` assert then fails every create).

Validated before-create guard example:

```json
{"key": "ticket_create_guard", "name": "Ticket create guard", "object_key": "ticket", "enabled": true,
 "trigger": {"phase": "before", "operation": "create"},
 "instructions": [{"key": "assert_initial_status_new", "type": "assert", "on_error": "fail",
   "config": {"source": "$candidate.status", "operator": "eq", "value": "new"}}],
 "execution": {"idempotency_keys": ["request_no"]}}
```

Choose the phase and instruction from the required business consequence:

| Requirement | Use | Do not use it for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Reject the current write when an invariant fails | `before` + `assert` | External reads/effects or a later compensating check |
| Deterministically normalize fields on the current write | `before` + `derive_fields` | Multi-record mutation, repository access, or network I/O |
| Run a published business command after the record is committed | `after` + `invoke_business_action` | Rolling back the originating write |
| Start a long-lived, waiting, or human process from committed state | `after` + `start_workflow` | Immediate validation or atomic mutation |
| Publish a durable domain signal from committed state | `after` + `emit_event` | A synchronous guard or an arbitrary-recipient notification |

The trigger `operation` is exactly `create`, `update`, `delete`, or `transition`. `changed_fields` is valid only for `update`; `from_state` and `to_state` are valid only for `transition`.

Condition clause operators are exactly `empty`, `eq`, `future_date`, `gt`, `gte`, `in`, `lt`, `lte`, `ne`, and `not_empty`. Use `eq`, never `equals`; use `ne`, never `not_equals`.

`trigger.phase`, not `execution.mode`, selects the transaction boundary. A `before` rule executes synchronously inside the current mutation using only in-memory conditions and deterministic payload transforms; two rules deriving different values for the same field block with a write conflict. An `after` rule is placed on the durable outbox after persistence, revalidates the initiating user and role when consumed, and cannot roll back the originating write. Do not set `mode:"sync"` on an `after` rule to imply pre-commit execution, and do not set `mode:"async"` on a `before` rule. `execution.result_notification` (`none`, `failures`, or `all`) reports the terminal after-rule result to the initiator; it is not a business notification recipient selector.

`execution.idempotency_keys` is specifically the field tuple used to find a replay of a matching `before` + `create` rule. Every key must be a declared field on `object_key`. There is no implicit project-object `id` field. Use stable required business keys such as `request_no`, and do not put `idempotency_keys` on an after rule expecting it to control after-rule deduplication. Runtime derives after outbox and per-instruction idempotency from rule, object, record, operation, and record version.

The published instruction shape accepts `on_error:"continue"|"fail"`, but the current Runtime execution loop blocks the rule at the first instruction error and does not branch on `on_error`. Use `fail` for authored rules. If the requirement genuinely needs best-effort continuation, record a Runtime automation owner gap instead of claiming that `continue` is effective.

## Reuse, extension, and prohibitions
Use automation for event-driven behavior. Use Workflow when the behavior waits, assigns humans, or has a long-lived lifecycle. Use one transactional Action/Handler when the originating operation and multiple record mutations must succeed or fail together. Do not hide a multi-record atomic transaction in after automation.

## Examples
Correct after-write audit/event evidence:

```json
{"key":"financial_audit","name":"Financial audit","object_key":"sales_order","enabled":true,"trigger":{"phase":"after","operation":"update","changed_fields":["status"]},"conditions":{"mode":"all","clauses":[{"reference":"$record.status","operator":"not_empty"}]},"instructions":[{"key":"emit_financial_change","type":"emit_event","on_error":"fail","config":{"event_type":"sales_order.financial_state_changed","object_key":"sales_order","record_id":"$record.id"}}],"execution":{"mode":"async","run_as":"initiator","result_notification":"failures","timeout_seconds":30,"max_depth":4},"audit_event":"automation.sales_order.financial_state_changed"}
```

The following missing instruction variants are copied from the published Runtime authoring shapes, with `on_error:"fail"` to match current execution semantics:

<!-- code-example: automation-instructions -->
```json
[
  {"phase":"before","instruction":{"key":"derive","type":"derive_fields","name":"Derive work state","on_error":"fail","config":{"fields":{"status":"ready","automation_source":"runtime"}}}},
  {"phase":"after","instruction":{"key":"complete","type":"invoke_business_action","name":"Complete work","on_error":"fail","config":{"action_key":"work_item.complete","object_key":"work_item","record_id":"$record.id","input":{"source":"automation"}}}},
  {"phase":"after","instruction":{"key":"approval","type":"start_workflow","name":"Start approval","on_error":"fail","config":{"workflow_key":"work_item.approval","payload":{"record_id":"$record.id"}}}}
]
```

`derive_fields` is a before-persistence candidate transform; `invoke_business_action` and `start_workflow` are after-persistence effects. Swapping those phases fails the Runtime instruction-shape validator. The referenced Action or Workflow must still be declared by the complete model.

Correct: reject an invalid state transition with `before` + `assert`. Correct: after member creation emit a durable `member.created` event. Wrong: asynchronously decrement class capacity after booking commit; use one transactional Action. Wrong: use `idempotency_keys:["status"]` on an after rule to request per-status deduplication. Wrong: `{ "phase":"after", "event":"update", "instructions":[{"type":"audit"}] }`.

## Authority and limits
Contract and validation: `internal/runtime/domain/automation/policy/automation_authoring_policy.go`, `internal/runtime/domain/automation/validation/automation_authoring_fragment_validator.go`, and `internal/runtime/domain/manifest/validation/manifest_validator_automation.go`.

Execution semantics: `internal/runtime/application/automation/automation_before_application_service.go`, `internal/runtime/application/automation/automation_record_lifecycle_application_service.go`, `internal/runtime/application/automation/automation_rule_application_service.go`, and `internal/runtime/application/automation/automation_instruction_execution_application_service.go`.
# Scheduler

> **TL;DR** — Owns: scheduled jobs, calendar/interval expressions, scheduled-Workflow dispatch, report-export scheduling, retry/missed-window policy. Read when: time-driven recurring or delayed work exists. Never: build a project cron daemon.

## Problem and owner
Runtime scheduler owns timed definitions and run/retry/cancel/dead-letter execution lifecycle.

## Supported model and Blueprint expression
Declare schedule, target, retry limits and permissions. Runtime records jobs and execution outcomes and exposes operational control. The current Blueprint contract supports exactly two `target_type` values: `workflow` and `report_export`; `target_key` must reference the matching declared collection. Direct Action/CRUD targets are not authorable Scheduler targets: wrap timed domain work in a declared Workflow, whose Action node invokes the project Action. That target Workflow uses `trigger_contract.type:"scheduled"`; never invent `timer` as a Workflow trigger type because Scheduler owns the timing expression and `timer` is only a graph-node contract.

Every scheduled job requires `key`, `name`, `status`, `target_type`, `target_key`, object-valued `schedule`, `missed_window_policy`, `max_attempts`, and `timeout_seconds`. Status is `draft|enabled|paused|disabled`; missed-window policy is `skip|catch_up_one|catch_up_bounded`. `catch_up_bounded` additionally requires `max_catchup_windows`. Schedule variants are `cron` (`expression`, optional `timezone`), `interval` (`interval_seconds`), `daily_at` (`time_of_day`, optional `timezone`), `weekly_at` (`time_of_day`, `day_of_week`, optional `timezone`), or `monthly_at` (`time_of_day`, `day_of_month`, optional `timezone`). Do not use string-valued `schedule`, top-level `timezone`, `target`, or `retry_policy`.

Choose the schedule by the business clock:

| Requirement | Schedule |
| --- | --- |
| Fixed elapsed cadence independent of local calendar | `interval` |
| Same local wall-clock time every day, week, or month | `daily_at`, `weekly_at`, or `monthly_at` with an explicit IANA `timezone` |
| Calendar expression not representable by those variants | `cron`; keep it to the Runtime-supported five-field/descriptor contract |

Prefer the named wall-clock variants over cron when both express the requirement; their intent and timezone are reviewable. Runtime defaults a missing timezone to UTC. For `monthly_at`, a `day_of_month` beyond the month's length runs on that month's last day, so use 31 only when “last available calendar day” is acceptable.

Choose missed-window behavior from the consequence of Runtime downtime:

| Policy | Runtime consequence | Choose when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `skip` | Drops missed windows, runs the current recovery occurrence, and advances from now | The target reconciles current state or old windows must not create duplicate/stale effects |
| `catch_up_one` | Executes the oldest due window once, then advances from now | One post-recovery reconciliation is required but every missed interval is not |
| `catch_up_bounded` | Discards backlog older than the bound, then replays the most recent `max_catchup_windows` in window order | Each recent window is a real business obligation and the target is window-idempotent |

Missed-window recovery and execution retry are different axes. `missed_window_policy` handles occurrences that were never claimed while the scheduler was unavailable; `max_attempts` and retry backoff handle failure of one claimed window. Do not increase retries to simulate catch-up, and do not use bounded catch-up for a non-idempotent notification, charge, or export unless the target deduplicates by the scheduled window. Runtime assigns scheduled runs a per-definition/per-window identity, but the downstream Workflow/Action must still preserve its own business idempotency.

Every `report_export` scheduled job additionally requires one `report_export_controls[]` entry whose `report_key` equals the job's `target_key`. The control requires `key`, `report_key`, non-empty `source_objects`, `audit_object`, `download_object`, `export_action`, `max_rows` of at least 1, and `reason`; optional approval, masking and watermark flags refine governance. Scheduling a report without this control is invalid even when the report itself is declared.

## Reuse, extension, and prohibitions
Use Scheduler to start a declared Workflow or export a declared report. Do not build a project cron daemon and do not claim a direct Action target that the authoring contract does not publish.

Acceptance follows the authenticated live `/openapi.json`; inspect it once and reuse its exact paths instead of guessing. The current manual operation is `POST /operations/scheduler/definitions/{definitionID}/run`, not `/scheduler/jobs/{definitionID}/run`. It is an Operations Surface command and therefore needs the published Operations permission and high-risk reason/confirmation contract; the permission key Runtime honors for it is `scheduler.command` (or `workspace.admin`/`job_run.update`) — a role modeled with only `scheduler.definition.run` gets 403, so grant `scheduler.command` to the operating role at model time. When the business acceptance actor cannot access it, exercise automatic catch-up/timer dispatch rather than weakening authorization. Then require the job run to reach a terminal success state and its target Workflow/Action to produce durable business effects, receipts, audit, and outbox as declared. A created job run in `retrying`, a `configuration_error` Workflow, or zero business evidence fails even when the scheduler cursor advanced.

A Workflow target is compiled as `scheduled:<workflow_key>` and targeted dispatch is fail-closed: a missing, disabled, or non-scheduled Workflow is an execution error, never a successful no-op. For a global scheduled Workflow whose `trigger_contract` has no `object_key`, Runtime starts the graph exactly once for the claimed Scheduler run; the graph Action node must carry its own explicit `object_key` and invoke the project Action as an object operation. For a record-scoped scheduled Workflow, declare `trigger_contract.object_key`; Runtime evaluates matching records and a zero-match scan may be a legitimate success. Do not add a fake trigger object to make a global reconciliation job run.

For every scheduled Workflow acceptance, correlate the Scheduler run with a durable Workflow execution. If the graph invokes a project Action, also prove its committed business effect after an independent read. An Action error must remain visible on the failed Workflow execution and force the Scheduler run to `retrying` or `dead_letter` according to `max_attempts`; a Scheduler `succeeded` response with no Workflow execution or no required Action effect is a release failure.

## Authority and limits

# Reports

> **TL;DR** — Owns: object analytics/Reports, `object_sql_v1` authoring, bounded pagination and threshold routing, governed export, fingerprint replay. Read when: a page or API returns Report rows or offers Report export. Never: unbounded/browser pagination or a separate count-only query.

## Problem and owner
Runtime report capability owns governed Dataset summary/snapshot and restricted `object_sql_v1` query/export boundaries.

Reports consume accepted domain facts; they do not decide or recreate those facts. Complete domain truth inside `requirements` before choosing an execution form.

| Demand | Required design |
| --- | --- |
| Simple single-object or fixed-dimension aggregation | Governed Dataset |
| Complex JOIN, CTE, window function, or special aggregation | Author-written native SQL file; use `object_sql_v1` only when the active Runtime supports every required construct, otherwise record a Report Runtime owner gap |
| Checkout, commission, points, inventory cost, or payroll locking | Atomic Action + Calculation Snapshot + immutable Ledger first; Report only aggregates those facts |
| Hypothetical rule or parameter trial | Separate Simulation; never write into official Reports or ledgers |

Never build a project-specific Report AST, metric DSL, or SQL generator. Runtime's internal parsing and semantic binding are security implementation details, not an authoring surface. Never make a Report join current Settings to replay historical financial calculations.

Current compatibility boundary: `sql_file` improves source ownership but does not widen `object_sql_v1`. The current P0 Runtime accepts bounded SELECT/JOIN/GROUP BY/HAVING/ORDER BY and rejects author CTEs, subqueries, UNION, and windows. When a truthful report needs a rejected construct, keep it as an explicit Runtime Report owner gap; do not force it into Dataset, rewrite the domain facts, or claim the Skill supports unrestricted native SQL. The follow-up platform owner is Runtime Report authoring/execution and must preserve permission, RLS, read-only execution, parameter binding, resource limits, export-scope parity, and source-file hash provenance.

## Supported model and Blueprint expression
Every Report declares exactly one execution definition: a governed `dataset`, or `object_sql_v1` with canonical SQL, declared source objects, typed parameters, result schema, optional join cardinalities, and timeout. In `backend/model/*.json`, native SQL uses one matching `sql_file:"backend/reports/<report-key>.sql"` instead of inline `sql`; the V2 model loader normalizes and hashes that project-owned file and embeds it into the same published `sql` contract. Frontends consume only the corresponding typed Runtime Client operation; Object SQL never falls back to Dataset or browser/in-memory evaluation.

## List pagination and export lifecycle

These are non-negotiable Report design checks: bounded server pagination for list rows; one permission-filtered bounded threshold probe of the identical Report contract; fixed export routing at 1000; terminal exact total; atomic canonical-fingerprint replay; and requester-only completed/failed Inbox notification for the asynchronous branch. Complete them before selecting Report metadata or implementation.

Any Report response that returns list rows must expose bounded server pagination. Its thin contract names either the platform standard or `page_size` plus an opaque `cursor`, the maximum page size, a deterministic stable sort and stable cursor with a unique tie-breaker bound into the cursor, and explicit `truncated` and `total` semantics. A valid observable tie-breaker may be one unique dimension in ascending or descending order, or the complete strictly monotonic dimension tuple; repeated or order-reversing tuples are not proof. `total` may be exact, estimated, or omitted, but the response and PRD must say which. `truncated` distinguishes a bounded partial result from an exhausted result. Never return an unbounded list, fetch all rows into the browser, or call slicing in browser memory “pagination.”

Every Report export prepare must probe the same Report under normalized parameters and current authorization/data Scope. The fixed routing threshold is 1000: an exhausted bounded probe from 0 through 1000 yields the exact total and returns the synchronous governed CSV; observing row 1001 is sufficient to enqueue the asynchronous export-job substrate without a separate `COUNT(*)` or full materialization. The worker reads the same Report contract in bounded database pages and records the final exact total at terminal completion. Only the async completed/failed terminal transitions publish requester-only Inbox notifications linked through the job to export audit and artifact. Both branches keep governed artifact/download reauthorization, expiry, integrity, and audit. A worker that reruns the full Report for every output page does not satisfy this contract.

Server deduplication is mandatory and does not rely on UI debounce or caller-generated randomness. Canonical fingerprint inputs include Report key, normalized parameters, SQL/source hash, requester/workspace, authorization/data-Scope hash, format, and the frozen result version. Exclude `audit_id`: it records one request but does not change the exported result. When an equivalent click supplies a new audit, atomically link and close that audit against the original job/artifact; do not return an idempotency conflict, create another job/file/download, or emit another terminal notification. Database compare-and-create ensures concurrent equivalent requests return one identity. An accepted/running fingerprint returns its existing job. A completed fingerprint with an unexpired, intact, currently authorized artifact reuses that artifact/download. Failed/cancelled work, expired/corrupt artifacts, or a changed SQL/source/parameter/authorization Scope may create exactly one new execution.

Current transport surface: `GET /reports/{reportKey}/summary` and `POST /reports/{reportKey}/query` accept `page_size` plus an opaque cursor and return `page_size`, `next_cursor`, `truncated`, `total`, and `total_semantics`; the hard maximum is 200. `total_semantics` is `at_least` while a bounded page proves only a lower bound and becomes `exact` when traversal is exhausted. `POST /reports/{reportKey}/exports/{objectKey}/prepare` returns `200` for the governed synchronous artifact or `202 Accepted` plus `Location` for a requester-owned job; job status/cancel and governed download routes are published. This describes request and response shape only. Verify the active package separately for bounded execution, query-count and memory budgets, signed source-version/keyset cursor behavior, restart recovery, no duplicate/missing rows, replay, download reauthorization, and terminal notification.

Async reauthorization is part of that supported contract, not an implementation detail projects may bypass. Before page one and again at governed download, Runtime restores the job workspace into Identity context, resolves the current persisted user-role assignment and organization facts, resolves the same default business-profile facts used by HTTP prepare, and compares the frozen authorization/data-Scope hash. A manifest-only role, missing workspace context, or invented Product/Business Surface is not equivalent. True permission, assignment, organization, or business-profile drift fails closed; unchanged facts must not fail merely because execution moved from HTTP to a worker.

Governed export uses `POST /reports/{reportKey}/exports/{objectKey}/prepare`
with `audit_id` plus an immutable `scope`. The scope may name only declared
report dimension keys, measure keys, and analysis keys; it binds query identity,
filters, date dimension/range, IANA timezone, stable tag-family values plus their
`any|all` relation, projected result fields,
purpose, metric definition key/version assertions, freshness, and optional
current role/data-scope assertions. Runtime canonicalizes role, data scopes, and
metric definition versions from the authenticated principal and current report.
Unknown dimensions/operators/fields, arbitrary query fragments, mismatched
assertions, masked measures, and stale snapshot requirements fail closed.
`query_key` is executable only when it names one `dataset.query_predicates[]`
entry and `tags` may name only `dataset.tag_predicates[]` entries. Each entry is
a stable `key` plus 1..16 closed dataset `filters`; arbitrary SQL, expressions,
field names, or operators are never accepted from the request. Selected tag
predicates are canonicalized, deduplicated, sorted, and combined with AND. The
summary endpoint accepts the same `query_key` and repeated `tags` parameters so
the visible page and prepared CSV execute one predicate contract. Governed
export additionally requires every selected key in the matching control's
`allowed_query_keys` or `allowed_tags`; empty control allowlists grant nothing.
Unknown keys/tags/operators and snapshot selector overrides fail closed. A realtime request timezone is
executable: date-only bounds are converted from that IANA timezone to exact UTC
instants and time buckets use the same scoped timezone. Snapshot exports reject
a timezone override that differs from the report snapshot definition.

The published Prepare route performs the bounded authorized threshold probe and
binds the result identity. An exhausted 0-through-1000-row probe synchronously
persists and returns the governed CSV (zero rows produce the valid header-only
artifact); observing row 1001 returns the requester-owned job. The current
Runtime bounded path pushes `LIMIT page_size+1` plus a hard result maximum into
supported Dataset and `object_sql_v1` execution, appends deterministic tie
terms, signs the authorized source version into continuation cursors, and
rejects stale cursors instead of silently duplicating or omitting rows. The
async worker fences that source version, commits immutable chunks with its
checkpoint, and resumes without re-running a complete Report or calling prepare
again. Unsupported complex Dataset shapes fail closed with
`backend.report.bounded_page_unavailable`; a declared hard maximum may use full
execution only when it is at most the synchronous threshold, never for an async
claim. Active-delivery `pagination_trace`, cohort-driver `query_profile` (SQLite `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN`, MySQL `EXPLAIN FORMAT=JSON`, or PostgreSQL `EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON)`),
restart and artifact evidence remain mandatory. Watermarking remains governed
when configured.
The synchronous response carries artifact/content-hash headers; a completed
asynchronous job exposes its artifact ID, download token, expiry, and content
hash. `content_sha256` is SHA-256 of the exact final bytes returned by
`GET /report-exports/downloads/{token}`. Every download rechecks the
requester/workspace, expiry, current report/control/object/field permission,
authorization/data-scope fingerprint, definition hashes, immutable scope hash,
and file hash, and audits success, denial, or expiry. A project Action's legacy
`download_id` or metadata `content_hash` is not a Runtime download token or file
hash; continue the handoff through prepare and use only its returned token/hash.
The audit Action creates only a request record in a prepare-eligible status such
as `requested`. `record_mapping` declares the accepted request statuses plus the
Runtime-owned prepared/downloaded/denied/expired status values and audit
row-count/scope-hash fields. Runtime writes prepared status, actual grouped CSV
row count, and `sha256:<normalized-scope-hash>` in one record update only after
governed artifact bytes exist; it never trusts a client-provided filters hash.
Download success writes downloaded, rejected prepare writes denied, and an
expired token writes expired. Zero rows are a successful synchronous export,
not a denial.

The route surface is not proof of production execution semantics. If Report list or export is in the frozen requirement scope, it cannot be marked not applicable or silently excluded: the active delivery must pass the bounded execution, stable-cursor, managed-cohort query-profile and recovery cases; otherwise acceptance fails with the exact Runtime Report owner gap. If no Report list/export requirement exists, record the machine-derived not-applicable reason.

The Blueprint shape is exact. A Report emission repeats the same key in both places: `{"collection":"reports","key":"part_usage_report","value":{"key":"part_usage_report",...}}`; the emission envelope never supplies the required `value.key` for the SQL-file loader. A report value has top-level `key`, optional `name`/`i18n`, exactly one of `dataset` or `object_sql_v1`, and optional `required_permissions`, `audience_roles`, `evidence_requirements`, `materialization`, and `export_scope`. Dataset-owned fields must be nested under `dataset`: `source`, `joins`, `filters`, `query_predicates`, `tag_predicates`, `dimensions`, `measures`, `time_grain`, `time_zone`, `sort`, `limit`, `privacy`, `comparisons`, and `analyses`. Object SQL owns `sql`, `source_objects`, `parameters`, `result_schema`, `join_cardinalities`, and `timeout_milliseconds`. Do not put `object_key`, `dimensions`, `measures`, `filters`, `allowed_roles`, `description`, `snapshot_policy`, or `export_policy` at report top level.

Call `queryReportObjectSQL(reportKey, parameters, {pageSize, cursor})` for interactive Object SQL and continue only with the returned opaque `next_cursor`. Governed export passes the same declared values as `prepareReportExportRouted(..., {scope: {parameters, purpose, freshness:{mode:'realtime'}, ...}})`. Runtime canonicalizes defaults/types before scope hashing and audit, compiles the same SQL, injects the same RLS, checks the same read fields plus export permission, and reauthorizes on download. The preparing principal's role additionally needs `report_export_audit.update`, `report_export_download.create`, and data write permission on both the declared `audit_object` and `download_object`; grant these at model time or prepare fails 403. Dataset selectors (`query_key`, tags, filters, date range, analysis, timezone, metrics) are invalid for Object SQL; unknown parameters, arbitrary SQL, fields, or result columns fail closed. Keep deprecated `prepareReportExport`/`exportReportObject` only so previously generated adapters compile; never author new calls to them.

`dataset.source` requires both `object_key` and a non-empty local `alias`. A dimension requires `key` and `field: {"source_alias":"...","field_key":"..."}`. A measure requires `key` and `operation`; legal operations are `count`, `distinct_count`, `sum`, `avg`, `min`, `max`, `ratio`, `duration`, and `percentile`. A plain count needs no field. Field-based measures use `field`, not `field_key` or `aggregation`. Every alias referenced by fields and measures must be the source alias or a declared join alias.

A join keeps the legacy single-key form `left_field` + `right_field`, or uses
`field_equalities` with 1..8 unique `{left_field,right_field}` pairs; never mix
the two forms. Every pair is equality-only, references the join's `left_alias`
and joined `alias`, and requires the same read/export field checks and indexing
as a single-key join. `cardinality` remains required. Runtime rejects actual
right-key duplication for `many_to_one`, duplication on either side for
`one_to_one`, and plan-time additive-measure amplification across
`one_to_many`; it never silently aggregates a cardinality violation.

Every Object field used by a report join, filter, time-bucket dimension, or analysis entity/time/event field must be indexed. Set `"config":{"indexed":true}` on the declared Object field unless it is already `unique:true`; relation fields are indexed by default unless explicitly disabled. Runtime's physical recommendation is tenant-leading `workspace_id,<field_key>`. Dataset-level `time_grain` is a default for every dimension that omits its own grain, so do not set it on a dataset containing categorical dimensions such as `status`, `result`, or `method`; put `time_grain` only on the actual datetime dimension. Otherwise those categorical fields become time-bucket access paths and must also be indexed.

Omit `dataset.privacy` unless the report truly needs group suppression. When present, it is a closed object with exactly `minimum_group_size` (integer 2..1000) and `entity_field: {"source_alias":"...","field_key":"..."}`. The entity field must exist on the named dataset source/join alias and identifies the distinct privacy subject counted for suppression. `mask_sensitive_fields` is not a report privacy property; field masking remains owned by Runtime CLS and export policy.

`report_export_controls[]` is also closed. Use `masking_required` for the export masking flag, never `mask_sensitive_fields`. Its declared fields are `key`, `name`, `i18n`, `report_key`, `source_objects`, `sensitive_source_objects`, `sensitive_field_policy_keys`, `object_export_policy_keys`, `approval_required`, `masking_required`, `watermark`, `audit_object`, `download_object`, `record_mapping`, `export_action`, `allowed_query_keys`, `allowed_tags`, `max_rows`, `reason`, and optional `config`. Required `record_mapping` keys are `audit_report_key_field`, `audit_requester_field`, `audit_status_field`, `audit_prepared_statuses`, `audit_prepared_status`, `audit_downloaded_status`, `audit_denied_status`, `audit_expired_status`, `audit_row_count_field`, `audit_scope_hash_field`, `download_audit_field`, `download_filename_field`, `download_content_hash_field`, and `download_expires_at_field`; token/watermark/download-number field mappings are optional.

Preflight export authorization as one requesting principal, not as grants spread across roles. At least one role must simultaneously have the Report audience and required permissions, the export Action grant, `<source>.export` plus source data read for every source Object, `<audit_object>.update` plus audit data write, and `<download_object>.create` plus download data write. Also give the emitted `export_action` a matching `business_handler` behavior owner; governance/helper Actions are not exempt from reverse behavior ownership.

## Reuse, extension, and prohibitions
Use Runtime reports for governed analytics. Do not fetch all records into the browser, paginate in browser memory, or bypass export permissions. The legitimate synchronous `<=1000` prepare response is Runtime-governed; it is not permission to create CSV in the browser or call the removed backing-record route. Do not use generic batch download, add a second query, vary the threshold, or generate another artifact for an equivalent fingerprint.

Summary, detail, page, payroll, and export must share the same authoritative facts and permission/data scope. Do not repeat formulas in any consumer, zero-fill a missing/unproven fact, or omit ledger-ID-level traceability where a ledger exists. Settings changes must not drift historical results.

Correct minimal governed summary:

```json

  "key":"member_status_summary","name":"Member status summary",
  "dataset":{
    "source":{"object_key":"gym_member","alias":"member"},
    "dimensions":[{"key":"status","field":{"source_alias":"member","field_key":"status"}}],

  },

  "materialization":{"maximum_lag_seconds":300,"consistency_retries":3}
}
```

Wrong: `{"object_key":"gym_member","dimensions":[{"field_key":"status"}],"measures":[{"aggregation":"count"}],"allowed_roles":["gym_manager"]}`. Those are not the Runtime Report contract. Wrong: unrestricted CSV from a custom endpoint; use governed report export.

If a truthful business requirement needs a Report result cap, `dataset.limit` may declare that cap, but it is never pagination evidence and must not be set to 1000 merely because export routing uses a 1000-row threshold.

Correct privacy fragment: `"privacy":{"minimum_group_size":2,"entity_field":{"source_alias":"member","field_key":"member_no"}}`. Wrong: `"privacy":{"minimum_group_size":0,"entity_field":"member_no","mask_sensitive_fields":true}`.

## Authority and limits

## object_sql_v1 authoring contract (validated against the shipped compiler)

The SQL is compiled by a **vitess (MySQL-dialect) parser** with a closed plan contract; every rule below fails `model plan` (`backend.report.object_sql_*`). The parser dialect governs authoring syntax only — execution and acceptance run on the current managed Runtime cohort's `database_driver`; never provision another database engine for this. This MySQL parser wording is an authoring-syntax fact, not an acceptance-engine requirement:

- **Reserved identifiers need backticks**: an object named `lead`, `order`, `group`, etc. collides with MySQL keywords — write ``FROM `lead` AS l``. Double quotes are NOT identifier quotes in this dialect.
- **Exactly one joined source tree**, and **every FROM/JOIN source requires an explicit alias** (`FROM `lead` AS l`). Each joined alias (not the root alias) needs exactly one `join_cardinalities` contract entry with the closed shape `{"alias":"joined_alias","cardinality":"many_to_one"}`. Only `alias` and `cardinality` are allowed; `left_alias`/`right_alias` belong to Dataset joins and are invalid here.
- **Every SELECT column requires an explicit alias that exactly equals the corresponding `result_schema[i].key`**, in order, no `SELECT *`: `SELECT l.company_name AS company_name, ...`.
- **`result_schema` entries require BOTH `type` and `kind`**. `kind` is `dimension` or `measure`. `type` is the closed enum `text`, `integer`, `number`, `decimal`, `boolean`, `date`, `datetime`, `currency` — object field types such as `phone`, `user`, `relation`, `select` are NOT result types; declare them as `text` in the result schema (the object field declaration is unaffected).
- Declared `source_objects` must exactly cover the objects referenced in FROM/JOINs; the declared column type must be compatible with the compiled expression type.
- **Declare an explicit `ORDER BY` plus a literal `LIMIT` in `1..10000`** sized to the business bound: the compiled query otherwise applies a default `LIMIT 1000`, which equals the 1000/1001 sync/async export threshold, so a >1000-row report silently truncates to exactly 1000 rows in a synchronous export (database-agnostic rule). Values above 10000 fail `backend.report.object_sql_limit_invalid`; do not use a large placeholder.

Validated minimal example:

```sql
SELECT l.company_name AS company_name, l.expected_amount AS expected_amount
FROM `lead` AS l
ORDER BY l.id
LIMIT 5000
```

with `"result_schema": [{"key":"company_name","type":"text","kind":"dimension"},{"key":"expected_amount","type":"currency","kind":"measure"}]`.

# Scheduler

> **TL;DR** — Owns: scheduled jobs, calendar/interval expressions, scheduled-Workflow dispatch, report-export scheduling, retry/missed-window policy. Read when: time-driven recurring or delayed work exists. Never: build a project cron daemon.

## Problem and owner
Runtime scheduler owns timed definitions and run/retry/cancel/dead-letter execution lifecycle.

## Supported model and Blueprint expression
Declare schedule, target, retry limits and permissions. Runtime records jobs and execution outcomes and exposes operational control. The current Blueprint contract supports exactly two `target_type` values: `workflow` and `report_export`; `target_key` must reference the matching declared collection. Direct Action/CRUD targets are not authorable Scheduler targets: wrap timed domain work in a declared Workflow, whose Action node invokes the project Action. That target Workflow uses `trigger_contract.type:"scheduled"`; never invent `timer` as a Workflow trigger type because Scheduler owns the timing expression and `timer` is only a graph-node contract.

Every scheduled job requires `key`, `name`, `status`, `target_type`, `target_key`, object-valued `schedule`, `missed_window_policy`, `max_attempts`, and `timeout_seconds`. Status is `draft|enabled|paused|disabled`; missed-window policy is `skip|catch_up_one|catch_up_bounded`. `catch_up_bounded` additionally requires `max_catchup_windows`. Schedule variants are `cron` (`expression`, optional `timezone`), `interval` (`interval_seconds`), `daily_at` (`time_of_day`, optional `timezone`), `weekly_at` (`time_of_day`, `day_of_week`, optional `timezone`), or `monthly_at` (`time_of_day`, `day_of_month`, optional `timezone`). Do not use string-valued `schedule`, top-level `timezone`, `target`, or `retry_policy`.

Choose the schedule by the business clock:

| Requirement | Schedule |
| --- | --- |
| Fixed elapsed cadence independent of local calendar | `interval` |
| Same local wall-clock time every day, week, or month | `daily_at`, `weekly_at`, or `monthly_at` with an explicit IANA `timezone` |
| Calendar expression not representable by those variants | `cron`; keep it to the Runtime-supported five-field/descriptor contract |

Prefer the named wall-clock variants over cron when both express the requirement; their intent and timezone are reviewable. Runtime defaults a missing timezone to UTC. For `monthly_at`, a `day_of_month` beyond the month's length runs on that month's last day, so use 31 only when “last available calendar day” is acceptable.

Choose missed-window behavior from the consequence of Runtime downtime:

| Policy | Runtime consequence | Choose when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `skip` | Drops missed windows, runs the current recovery occurrence, and advances from now | The target reconciles current state or old windows must not create duplicate/stale effects |
| `catch_up_one` | Executes the oldest due window once, then advances from now | One post-recovery reconciliation is required but every missed interval is not |
| `catch_up_bounded` | Discards backlog older than the bound, then replays the most recent `max_catchup_windows` in window order | Each recent window is a real business obligation and the target is window-idempotent |

Missed-window recovery and execution retry are different axes. `missed_window_policy` handles occurrences that were never claimed while the scheduler was unavailable; `max_attempts` and retry backoff handle failure of one claimed window. Do not increase retries to simulate catch-up, and do not use bounded catch-up for a non-idempotent notification, charge, or export unless the target deduplicates by the scheduled window. Runtime assigns scheduled runs a per-definition/per-window identity, but the downstream Workflow/Action must still preserve its own business idempotency.

Every `report_export` scheduled job additionally requires one `report_export_controls[]` entry whose `report_key` equals the job's `target_key`. The control requires `key`, `report_key`, non-empty `source_objects`, `audit_object`, `download_object`, `export_action`, `max_rows` of at least 1, and `reason`; optional approval, masking and watermark flags refine governance. Scheduling a report without this control is invalid even when the report itself is declared.

## Reuse, extension, and prohibitions
Use Scheduler to start a declared Workflow or export a declared report. Do not build a project cron daemon and do not claim a direct Action target that the authoring contract does not publish.

Acceptance follows the authenticated live `/openapi.json`; inspect it once and reuse its exact paths instead of guessing. The current manual operation is `POST /operations/scheduler/definitions/{definitionID}/run`, not `/scheduler/jobs/{definitionID}/run`. It is an Operations Surface command and therefore needs the published Operations permission and high-risk reason/confirmation contract; the permission key Runtime honors for it is `scheduler.command` (or `workspace.admin`/`job_run.update`) — a role modeled with only `scheduler.definition.run` gets 403, so grant `scheduler.command` to the operating role at model time. When the business acceptance actor cannot access it, exercise automatic catch-up/timer dispatch rather than weakening authorization. Then require the job run to reach a terminal success state and its target Workflow/Action to produce durable business effects, receipts, audit, and outbox as declared. A created job run in `retrying`, a `configuration_error` Workflow, or zero business evidence fails even when the scheduler cursor advanced.

A Workflow target is compiled as `scheduled:<workflow_key>` and targeted dispatch is fail-closed: a missing, disabled, or non-scheduled Workflow is an execution error, never a successful no-op. For a global scheduled Workflow whose `trigger_contract` has no `object_key`, Runtime starts the graph exactly once for the claimed Scheduler run; the graph Action node must carry its own explicit `object_key` and invoke the project Action as an object operation. For a record-scoped scheduled Workflow, declare `trigger_contract.object_key`; Runtime evaluates matching records and a zero-match scan may be a legitimate success. Do not add a fake trigger object to make a global reconciliation job run.

For every scheduled Workflow acceptance, correlate the Scheduler run with a durable Workflow execution. If the graph invokes a project Action, also prove its committed business effect after an independent read. An Action error must remain visible on the failed Workflow execution and force the Scheduler run to `retrying` or `dead_letter` according to `max_attempts`; a Scheduler `succeeded` response with no Workflow execution or no required Action effect is a release failure.

## Authority and limits
Contract and projection: `internal/runtime/domain/scheduler/policy/scheduler_authoring_policy.go`, `internal/runtime/domain/scheduler/validation/scheduler_definition_validation.go`, and `internal/controlplane/blueprint/compiler/scheduler_projection.go`.

# Reports

> **TL;DR** — Owns: object analytics/Reports, `object_sql_v1` authoring, bounded pagination and threshold routing, governed export, fingerprint replay. Read when: a page or API returns Report rows or offers Report export. Never: unbounded/browser pagination or a separate count-only query.

## Problem and owner
Runtime report capability owns governed Dataset summary/snapshot and restricted `object_sql_v1` query/export boundaries.

Reports consume accepted domain facts; they do not decide or recreate those facts. Complete domain truth inside `requirements` before choosing an execution form.

| Demand | Required design |
| --- | --- |
| Simple single-object or fixed-dimension aggregation | Governed Dataset |
| Complex JOIN, CTE, window function, or special aggregation | Author-written native SQL file; use `object_sql_v1` only when the active Runtime supports every required construct, otherwise record a Report Runtime owner gap |
| Checkout, commission, points, inventory cost, or payroll locking | Atomic Action + Calculation Snapshot + immutable Ledger first; Report only aggregates those facts |
| Hypothetical rule or parameter trial | Separate Simulation; never write into official Reports or ledgers |

Never build a project-specific Report AST, metric DSL, or SQL generator. Runtime's internal parsing and semantic binding are security implementation details, not an authoring surface. Never make a Report join current Settings to replay historical financial calculations.

Current compatibility boundary: `sql_file` improves source ownership but does not widen `object_sql_v1`. The current P0 Runtime accepts bounded SELECT/JOIN/GROUP BY/HAVING/ORDER BY and rejects author CTEs, subqueries, UNION, and windows. When a truthful report needs a rejected construct, keep it as an explicit Runtime Report owner gap; do not force it into Dataset, rewrite the domain facts, or claim the Skill supports unrestricted native SQL. The follow-up platform owner is Runtime Report authoring/execution and must preserve permission, RLS, read-only execution, parameter binding, resource limits, export-scope parity, and source-file hash provenance.

## Supported model and Blueprint expression
Every Report declares exactly one execution definition: a governed `dataset`, or `object_sql_v1` with canonical SQL, declared source objects, typed parameters, result schema, optional join cardinalities, and timeout. In `backend/model/*.json`, native SQL uses one matching `sql_file:"backend/reports/<report-key>.sql"` instead of inline `sql`; the V2 model loader normalizes and hashes that project-owned file and embeds it into the same published `sql` contract. Frontends consume only the corresponding typed Runtime Client operation; Object SQL never falls back to Dataset or browser/in-memory evaluation.

## List pagination and export lifecycle

These are non-negotiable Report design checks: bounded server pagination for list rows; one permission-filtered bounded threshold probe of the identical Report contract; fixed export routing at 1000; terminal exact total; atomic canonical-fingerprint replay; and requester-only completed/failed Inbox notification for the asynchronous branch. Complete them before selecting Report metadata or implementation.

Any Report response that returns list rows must expose bounded server pagination. Its thin contract names either the platform standard or `page_size` plus an opaque `cursor`, the maximum page size, a deterministic stable sort and stable cursor with a unique tie-breaker bound into the cursor, and explicit `truncated` and `total` semantics. A valid observable tie-breaker may be one unique dimension in ascending or descending order, or the complete strictly monotonic dimension tuple; repeated or order-reversing tuples are not proof. `total` may be exact, estimated, or omitted, but the response and PRD must say which. `truncated` distinguishes a bounded partial result from an exhausted result. Never return an unbounded list, fetch all rows into the browser, or call slicing in browser memory “pagination.”

Every Report export prepare must probe the same Report under normalized parameters and current authorization/data Scope. The fixed routing threshold is 1000: an exhausted bounded probe from 0 through 1000 yields the exact total and returns the synchronous governed CSV; observing row 1001 is sufficient to enqueue the asynchronous export-job substrate without a separate `COUNT(*)` or full materialization. The worker reads the same Report contract in bounded database pages and records the final exact total at terminal completion. Only the async completed/failed terminal transitions publish requester-only Inbox notifications linked through the job to export audit and artifact. Both branches keep governed artifact/download reauthorization, expiry, integrity, and audit. A worker that reruns the full Report for every output page does not satisfy this contract.

Server deduplication is mandatory and does not rely on UI debounce or caller-generated randomness. Canonical fingerprint inputs include Report key, normalized parameters, SQL/source hash, requester/workspace, authorization/data-Scope hash, format, and the frozen result version. Exclude `audit_id`: it records one request but does not change the exported result. When an equivalent click supplies a new audit, atomically link and close that audit against the original job/artifact; do not return an idempotency conflict, create another job/file/download, or emit another terminal notification. Database compare-and-create ensures concurrent equivalent requests return one identity. An accepted/running fingerprint returns its existing job. A completed fingerprint with an unexpired, intact, currently authorized artifact reuses that artifact/download. Failed/cancelled work, expired/corrupt artifacts, or a changed SQL/source/parameter/authorization Scope may create exactly one new execution.

Current transport surface: `GET /reports/{reportKey}/summary` and `POST /reports/{reportKey}/query` accept `page_size` plus an opaque cursor and return `page_size`, `next_cursor`, `truncated`, `total`, and `total_semantics`; the hard maximum is 200. `total_semantics` is `at_least` while a bounded page proves only a lower bound and becomes `exact` when traversal is exhausted. `POST /reports/{reportKey}/exports/{objectKey}/prepare` returns `200` for the governed synchronous artifact or `202 Accepted` plus `Location` for a requester-owned job; job status/cancel and governed download routes are published. This describes request and response shape only. Verify the active package separately for bounded execution, query-count and memory budgets, signed source-version/keyset cursor behavior, restart recovery, no duplicate/missing rows, replay, download reauthorization, and terminal notification.

Async reauthorization is part of that supported contract, not an implementation detail projects may bypass. Before page one and again at governed download, Runtime restores the job workspace into Identity context, resolves the current persisted user-role assignment and organization facts, resolves the same default business-profile facts used by HTTP prepare, and compares the frozen authorization/data-Scope hash. A manifest-only role, missing workspace context, or invented Product/Business Surface is not equivalent. True permission, assignment, organization, or business-profile drift fails closed; unchanged facts must not fail merely because execution moved from HTTP to a worker.

Governed export uses `POST /reports/{reportKey}/exports/{objectKey}/prepare`
with `audit_id` plus an immutable `scope`. The scope may name only declared
report dimension keys, measure keys, and analysis keys; it binds query identity,
filters, date dimension/range, IANA timezone, stable tag-family values plus their
`any|all` relation, projected result fields,
purpose, metric definition key/version assertions, freshness, and optional
current role/data-scope assertions. Runtime canonicalizes role, data scopes, and
metric definition versions from the authenticated principal and current report.
Unknown dimensions/operators/fields, arbitrary query fragments, mismatched
assertions, masked measures, and stale snapshot requirements fail closed.
`query_key` is executable only when it names one `dataset.query_predicates[]`
entry and `tags` may name only `dataset.tag_predicates[]` entries. Each entry is
a stable `key` plus 1..16 closed dataset `filters`; arbitrary SQL, expressions,
field names, or operators are never accepted from the request. Selected tag
predicates are canonicalized, deduplicated, sorted, and combined with AND. The
summary endpoint accepts the same `query_key` and repeated `tags` parameters so
the visible page and prepared CSV execute one predicate contract. Governed
export additionally requires every selected key in the matching control's
`allowed_query_keys` or `allowed_tags`; empty control allowlists grant nothing.
Unknown keys/tags/operators and snapshot selector overrides fail closed. A realtime request timezone is
executable: date-only bounds are converted from that IANA timezone to exact UTC
instants and time buckets use the same scoped timezone. Snapshot exports reject
a timezone override that differs from the report snapshot definition.

The published Prepare route performs the bounded authorized threshold probe and
binds the result identity. An exhausted 0-through-1000-row probe synchronously
persists and returns the governed CSV (zero rows produce the valid header-only
artifact); observing row 1001 returns the requester-owned job. The current
Runtime bounded path pushes `LIMIT page_size+1` plus a hard result maximum into
supported Dataset and `object_sql_v1` execution, appends deterministic tie
terms, signs the authorized source version into continuation cursors, and
rejects stale cursors instead of silently duplicating or omitting rows. The
async worker fences that source version, commits immutable chunks with its
checkpoint, and resumes without re-running a complete Report or calling prepare
again. Unsupported complex Dataset shapes fail closed with
`backend.report.bounded_page_unavailable`; a declared hard maximum may use full
execution only when it is at most the synchronous threshold, never for an async
claim. Active-delivery `pagination_trace`, cohort-driver `query_profile` (SQLite `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN`, MySQL `EXPLAIN FORMAT=JSON`, or PostgreSQL `EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON)`),
restart and artifact evidence remain mandatory. Watermarking remains governed
when configured.
The synchronous response carries artifact/content-hash headers; a completed
asynchronous job exposes its artifact ID, download token, expiry, and content
hash. `content_sha256` is SHA-256 of the exact final bytes returned by
`GET /report-exports/downloads/{token}`. Every download rechecks the
requester/workspace, expiry, current report/control/object/field permission,
authorization/data-scope fingerprint, definition hashes, immutable scope hash,
and file hash, and audits success, denial, or expiry. A project Action's legacy
`download_id` or metadata `content_hash` is not a Runtime download token or file
hash; continue the handoff through prepare and use only its returned token/hash.
The audit Action creates only a request record in a prepare-eligible status such
as `requested`. `record_mapping` declares the accepted request statuses plus the
Runtime-owned prepared/downloaded/denied/expired status values and audit
row-count/scope-hash fields. Runtime writes prepared status, actual grouped CSV
row count, and `sha256:<normalized-scope-hash>` in one record update only after
governed artifact bytes exist; it never trusts a client-provided filters hash.
Download success writes downloaded, rejected prepare writes denied, and an
expired token writes expired. Zero rows are a successful synchronous export,
not a denial.

The route surface is not proof of production execution semantics. If Report list or export is in the frozen requirement scope, it cannot be marked not applicable or silently excluded: the active delivery must pass the bounded execution, stable-cursor, managed-cohort query-profile and recovery cases; otherwise acceptance fails with the exact Runtime Report owner gap. If no Report list/export requirement exists, record the machine-derived not-applicable reason.

The Blueprint shape is exact. A Report emission repeats the same key in both places: `{"collection":"reports","key":"part_usage_report","value":{"key":"part_usage_report",...}}`; the emission envelope never supplies the required `value.key` for the SQL-file loader. A report value has top-level `key`, optional `name`/`i18n`, exactly one of `dataset` or `object_sql_v1`, and optional `required_permissions`, `audience_roles`, `evidence_requirements`, `materialization`, and `export_scope`. Dataset-owned fields must be nested under `dataset`: `source`, `joins`, `filters`, `query_predicates`, `tag_predicates`, `dimensions`, `measures`, `time_grain`, `time_zone`, `sort`, `limit`, `privacy`, `comparisons`, and `analyses`. Object SQL owns `sql`, `source_objects`, `parameters`, `result_schema`, `join_cardinalities`, and `timeout_milliseconds`. Do not put `object_key`, `dimensions`, `measures`, `filters`, `allowed_roles`, `description`, `snapshot_policy`, or `export_policy` at report top level.

Call `queryReportObjectSQL(reportKey, parameters, {pageSize, cursor})` for interactive Object SQL and continue only with the returned opaque `next_cursor`. Governed export passes the same declared values as `prepareReportExportRouted(..., {scope: {parameters, purpose, freshness:{mode:'realtime'}, ...}})`. Runtime canonicalizes defaults/types before scope hashing and audit, compiles the same SQL, injects the same RLS, checks the same read fields plus export permission, and reauthorizes on download. The preparing principal's role additionally needs `report_export_audit.update`, `report_export_download.create`, and data write permission on both the declared `audit_object` and `download_object`; grant these at model time or prepare fails 403. Dataset selectors (`query_key`, tags, filters, date range, analysis, timezone, metrics) are invalid for Object SQL; unknown parameters, arbitrary SQL, fields, or result columns fail closed. Keep deprecated `prepareReportExport`/`exportReportObject` only so previously generated adapters compile; never author new calls to them.

`dataset.source` requires both `object_key` and a non-empty local `alias`. A dimension requires `key` and `field: {"source_alias":"...","field_key":"..."}`. A measure requires `key` and `operation`; legal operations are `count`, `distinct_count`, `sum`, `avg`, `min`, `max`, `ratio`, `duration`, and `percentile`. A plain count needs no field. Field-based measures use `field`, not `field_key` or `aggregation`. Every alias referenced by fields and measures must be the source alias or a declared join alias.

A join keeps the legacy single-key form `left_field` + `right_field`, or uses
`field_equalities` with 1..8 unique `{left_field,right_field}` pairs; never mix
the two forms. Every pair is equality-only, references the join's `left_alias`
and joined `alias`, and requires the same read/export field checks and indexing
as a single-key join. `cardinality` remains required. Runtime rejects actual
right-key duplication for `many_to_one`, duplication on either side for
`one_to_one`, and plan-time additive-measure amplification across
`one_to_many`; it never silently aggregates a cardinality violation.

Every Object field used by a report join, filter, time-bucket dimension, or analysis entity/time/event field must be indexed. Set `"config":{"indexed":true}` on the declared Object field unless it is already `unique:true`; relation fields are indexed by default unless explicitly disabled. Runtime's physical recommendation is tenant-leading `workspace_id,<field_key>`. Dataset-level `time_grain` is a default for every dimension that omits its own grain, so do not set it on a dataset containing categorical dimensions such as `status`, `result`, or `method`; put `time_grain` only on the actual datetime dimension. Otherwise those categorical fields become time-bucket access paths and must also be indexed.

Omit `dataset.privacy` unless the report truly needs group suppression. When present, it is a closed object with exactly `minimum_group_size` (integer 2..1000) and `entity_field: {"source_alias":"...","field_key":"..."}`. The entity field must exist on the named dataset source/join alias and identifies the distinct privacy subject counted for suppression. `mask_sensitive_fields` is not a report privacy property; field masking remains owned by Runtime CLS and export policy.

`report_export_controls[]` is also closed. Use `masking_required` for the export masking flag, never `mask_sensitive_fields`. Its declared fields are `key`, `name`, `i18n`, `report_key`, `source_objects`, `sensitive_source_objects`, `sensitive_field_policy_keys`, `object_export_policy_keys`, `approval_required`, `masking_required`, `watermark`, `audit_object`, `download_object`, `record_mapping`, `export_action`, `allowed_query_keys`, `allowed_tags`, `max_rows`, `reason`, and optional `config`. Required `record_mapping` keys are `audit_report_key_field`, `audit_requester_field`, `audit_status_field`, `audit_prepared_statuses`, `audit_prepared_status`, `audit_downloaded_status`, `audit_denied_status`, `audit_expired_status`, `audit_row_count_field`, `audit_scope_hash_field`, `download_audit_field`, `download_filename_field`, `download_content_hash_field`, and `download_expires_at_field`; token/watermark/download-number field mappings are optional.

Preflight export authorization as one requesting principal, not as grants spread across roles. At least one role must simultaneously have the Report audience and required permissions, the export Action grant, `<source>.export` plus source data read for every source Object, `<audit_object>.update` plus audit data write, and `<download_object>.create` plus download data write. Also give the emitted `export_action` a matching `business_handler` behavior owner; governance/helper Actions are not exempt from reverse behavior ownership.

## Reuse, extension, and prohibitions
Use Runtime reports for governed analytics. Do not fetch all records into the browser, paginate in browser memory, or bypass export permissions. The legitimate synchronous `<=1000` prepare response is Runtime-governed; it is not permission to create CSV in the browser or call the removed backing-record route. Do not use generic batch download, add a second query, vary the threshold, or generate another artifact for an equivalent fingerprint.

Summary, detail, page, payroll, and export must share the same authoritative facts and permission/data scope. Do not repeat formulas in any consumer, zero-fill a missing/unproven fact, or omit ledger-ID-level traceability where a ledger exists. Settings changes must not drift historical results.

## Examples
Correct minimal governed summary:

```json
{
  "key":"member_status_summary","name":"Member status summary",
  "dataset":{
    "source":{"object_key":"gym_member","alias":"member"},
    "dimensions":[{"key":"status","field":{"source_alias":"member","field_key":"status"}}],
    "measures":[{"key":"members","operation":"count","source_alias":"member"}]
  },
  "audience_roles":["gym_manager"],
  "required_permissions":["gym_member.read"],
  "evidence_requirements":[{"object_key":"gym_member","minimum_records":1,"required_non_empty_fields":["status"]}],
  "materialization":{"maximum_lag_seconds":300,"consistency_retries":3}
}
```

Wrong: `{"object_key":"gym_member","dimensions":[{"field_key":"status"}],"measures":[{"aggregation":"count"}],"allowed_roles":["gym_manager"]}`. Those are not the Runtime Report contract. Wrong: unrestricted CSV from a custom endpoint; use governed report export.

If a truthful business requirement needs a Report result cap, `dataset.limit` may declare that cap, but it is never pagination evidence and must not be set to 1000 merely because export routing uses a 1000-row threshold.

Correct privacy fragment: `"privacy":{"minimum_group_size":2,"entity_field":{"source_alias":"member","field_key":"member_no"}}`. Wrong: `"privacy":{"minimum_group_size":0,"entity_field":"member_no","mask_sensitive_fields":true}`.

Correct indexed report field: `{"key":"occurred_at","name":"Occurred at","type":"datetime","required":true,"config":{"indexed":true}}`, used by `{"key":"day","field":{"source_alias":"access","field_key":"occurred_at"},"time_grain":"day"}`. Wrong: a dataset-level `"time_grain":"day"` shared by categorical `result` and `method` dimensions.

Correct compound current-version join: `{"alias":"current_version","object_key":"order_version","type":"inner","left_alias":"order","field_equalities":[{"left_field":"id","right_field":"order_id"},{"left_field":"version_counter","right_field":"version_no"}],"cardinality":"one_to_one"}`. Wrong: keeping only the ID equality and filtering a version number from a different alias, which can amplify unrelated versions.
